#2037. Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the big positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

Signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the new year.

Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj

His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

It was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

Before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15

PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr

Villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

It became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

PSG (4-3-3): Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes (Hernandez 75), Neves (Ruiz 75), Vitinha, Emery, Akliouche, (Dembele 45), Doue (Mayulu 87), Kvaratskhelia (Buraldo 88).Substitutes: Chevalier (g), Zabarnyi, Digne, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.Villa (4-2-3-1): Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres (Mings 80), Maatsen, Kamara (Bogarde 72), Gomes (Barkley 79), McGinn 7 (Alysson 73), Buendia, Hemmings, Madjo (Abraham 72).Substitutes: Wright (g), Asemota (g), Barkley, Nedeljkovic, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.Booked: Gomes, Torres, McGinn.Referee: Omar Artan (Somalia).

After the officials and the Aston Villa players receive their medals, it is time for the 2026 Uefa Super Cup winners PSG to receive their medals. The last man up is their captain Marquinhos, who has won a staggering 40 trophies during his time at PSG. He takes the trophy from Uefa President Aleksander Ceferin and lifts it above his head alongside his teammates.

PSG are your 2026 UEFA Super Cup Champions 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/1qCKEQ0IPK

Both Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have been heavily linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and neither player came off the bench for PSG tonight. Does that indicate that potentially those moves could be close, with neither played risked of picking up an injury?

Luis Enrique has now won 13 trophies with PSG. Serial winner 🏆 pic.twitter.com/RAsyI1Ui2s

💬 "We are ALWAYS hungry you know... we want more, we want more" Désiré Doué reflects on PSG's UEFA Super Cup Final win.📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nwreU1Skz7

Aston Villa will take on Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday in their final game of pre-season before they take on Brighton on the south coast on the opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

PSG play Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before they kick off the defence of their Ligue 1 crown at home against Rennes.

Possession: PSG 61%- Aston Villa 39%Shots: 12-15Shots on target: 6-4Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 29-34

Buendia has a late chance to equalise for Aston Villa from Maatsen’s cross but his header goes wide.

Not long after, the final whistle goes and PSG win the Super Cup for the second straight year. Last year they beat Tottenham on penalties, this time they beat Aston Villa 2-1. Unai Emery’s side acquitted themselves well and will regret some of their missed chances tonight. An entertaining affair in Salzburg.

PSG win back-to-back UEFA Super Cup's following goals from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vzMx6rGjuo

Dembele feeds a pass into the Villa box looking to pick out the run of Hakimi but there is slightly too much on it and Bizot is out to gather.

Into the final minute of added time we go.

Aston Villa are running out of time to find a late equaliser.

Maatsen brings Dembele down not far outside the Aston Villa box but play goes on as the latter gets up and shoots, with his effort saved by Bizot.

One final change for PSG as their other goalscorer tonight, Kvaratskhelia, is replaced by Beraldo. A defender comes on for an attacker as Luis Enrique’s side look to hold on for the victory.

Mayulu is coming on for Doue, whose goal may well have won back-to-back Super Cups for PSG.

The ball falls to Kvaratskhelia on the right side of the box and the Georgian chips it over Bizot but Cash is on hand to clear. Aston Villa then counter and Abraham feeds a pass forward at the perfect time to pick out the run of Alysson into the PSG box. Alysson then plays it across the six-yard box but neither Abraham nor Maatsen are there to meet the cross.

Double change for Aston Villa as Barkley and Mings replace Gomes and Torres, who were both on yellow cards.

Alysson, only just on the pitch, does brilliantly down Aston Villa’s right and drives into the PSG penalty area. His cross is parried away by Safonov straight into the path of Gomes, whose shot is blocked by Zaire-Emery.

PSG are making a double substitution as Ruiz and L Hernandez come on. Neves and Mendes, who had been struggling with cramp, go off.

Aston Villa are going to make a triple change as Abraham, Alysson and Bogarde come on. 17-year-old Madjo is one of those to be replaced as is McGinn, who has been booked as he goes off. The Aston Villa captain is distinctly unimpressed with the officials.

The space opens up for Mendes to take on the shot from range and he obliges, forcing Bizot into a decent save. Kvaratskhelia is unable to make contact with the follow-up. Mendes seems to be struggling with some cramp.

We are nearly 70 minutes into the game but Unai Emery has still not turned to his bench yet.

Aston Villa have an immediate chance to equalise through Hemmings but the 19-year-old’s effort from inside the box is straight at Safonov. That was a big chance for Hemmings.

Down the other end, Gomes is booked for a challenge from behind on Doue.

The VAR has checked it and there was no offside so the original decision is overturned and the goal is given. Doue is played in behind by Dembele down the right channel and is played onside by Cash on the far side. Doue takes it into the Villa penalty area and gets it onto his left foot. He curls it past Bizot and into the far corner.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj

Doue has the ball in the Aston Villa net but the offside flag has gone up. However, has Cash played Doue onside?

Cash’s cross from the right picks out Buendia at the front post but the latter’s header is off target. Unai Emery will be pretty happy with his side’s performance through the hour mark.

Mendes is a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul on McGinn as the Aston Villa captain spun the Portuguese defender on halfway. The referee must have thought both players had a hold of each other but I would lean towards Mendes probably fouling McGinn.

Other than 10/15 minutes in and around Kvaratskhelia’s goal, Aston Villa have put in a good performance and have created more chances than PSG. If anything, it will be Villa who will be disappointed that they have not scored more than once.

Just inside the PSG penalty area, McGinn cuts onto his left to get his shot away and his deflected effort is saved by Safonov diving to his right.

One of Aston Villa’s coaches has been booked for some protestations after Torres is penalised for a foul on Doue. Torres is also booked for that challenge.

Two of Aston Villa’s best players tonight thus far have been teenagers; 19-year-old Hemmings and 17-year-old Madjo. Aston Villa have seen some key, senior players depart this summer but will take joy from the performances of this pair.

Luis Enrique has decided he needed to make a change at the break as Dembele replaces Akliouche, who was quiet on his official debut for PSG after his move from Monaco.

Incredible to think he is only 17 years and 212 days old. He’s been all over PSG centre-back Willian Pacho and thoroughly deserves his goal.

The teenager could even have had a hat-trick. What a second-half this could be.

Madjo has managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s Georgian magician Kvicha Kvaratskhelia, which is quite some achievement.

Possession: PSG 67%-33% Aston VillaShots: 6-10Shots on target: 2-2Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 11-17

After one added minute, the first half is brought to an end and we are all square at 1-1 in Salzburg. Kvaratskhelia had put PSG in front but Madjo’s goal on the stroke of half-time has Aston Villa level at the break.

On the stroke of half-time, the 17-year-old levels for Aston Villa and finally takes his fourth big chance of the night. It is perhaps the hardest chance he has had as McGinn’s cross comes all the way to the back post. Madjo is being held by Pacho but somehow gets his foot to it and his shot goes into the roof of the net. What a moment for the 17-year-old!

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr

Madjo has his third massive chance of this first half and this shot comes off the post. Buendia feeds a pass forward into the path of Madjo, who appeared to be blocked by Pacho but he outmuscles him. Madjo then fires towards goal but it strikes the outside of the post. In a parallel universe, Madjo could have ahd a first-half hat-trick.

Aston Villa have had a few great chances in this first half and there is another. A free-kick into the PSG penalty area causes issues for the French side and Kamara’s header towards goal is saved by Safonov.

Madjo has his second huge chance of this first half. Once more it is McGinn who provides the cross. The Scot does really well on the right side of the box to fake the cross with his left and instead delivers with his right. He picks out Madjo at the back post and the 17-year-old should score but his header misses the target. What a story it would have been had the 17-year-old scored two goals against the Champions League winners.

Aston Villa have just settled things down. Either side of Kvaratskhelia’s goal, they were on the ropes but have calmed things down.

Hemmings is played in and he could potentially have gone down twice under challenges from Hakimi and then Mendes. The ball then falls to 17-year-old Madjo on the left side of the box. He opens up his body and tries to curl into the far corner but his effort goes wide.

Referees are now hot on players taking too long over throw-ins, with Mendes falling foul of that. That is one of the fairly new rules that will be good for the game.

A huge chance for 17-year-old Madjo to equalise. McGinn picks out the young striker with a sublime cross from the right. Madjo is just eight yards out and has a free header but it goes just wide of the far post. Aston Villa should be level.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15

After Aston Villa had made a solid start to this game, it is all PSG right now and Villa are on the ropes at the moment. PSG work it beautifully down their left after a sublime one-two between Mendes and Kvaratskhelia. Mendes drives down the left wing and has a cross into the box first-time which he declines. The Portuguese defender then has four different teammates that he could pick out in the penalty area but his cross misses all four.

PSG want a penalty. Kvaratskhelia shows great feet out on the left to drive into the Aston Villa penalty area. Gomes is on his back and Kvaratskhelia goes down. It did look like he was always looking to go down and it would have been very soft.

A few minutes after I said that Aston Villa had done a decent job of keeping PSG at bay, Luis Enrique’s side take the lead. Bizot had just made a great reflex save to deny Doue but he is unable to stop Kvaratskhelia’s effort. The Georgian cuts inside onto his right just inside the Aston Villa penalty area and gets his shot away quickly after quick feet. There is great venom on the shot and it beats Bizot, who thought Kvaratskhelia was going to go for the far corner but instead hit it at the near post. Could Bizot have saved that? Perhaps but Kvaratskhelia did belt that shot.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

As you would expect, PSG are dominating possession but thus far have been unable to create any genuine chances, much to Aston Villa’s credit. But, with the players PSG have at their disposal, they can cause chaos in a moment.

Tensions just start to simmer. McGinn gives a foul away on Mendes, who then attempts to take the free-kick a good few yards further forward from where it was. McGinn repeatedly tries to stop Mendes from taking it further forward before the referee steps in to end the dispute.

I don’t think we can take much from this result tonight, whatever it is. Villa cannot be properly judged until the window closes. Don’t bother telling that to Unai Emery, though. He is ready to continue defying the doubters.

The Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

Aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a big summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

“I feel like the club is in a new era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”

Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

“I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

“No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”

PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.

The goodwill towards David Storch and Arise Capital remains in place but they had to make the brave choice to sack Henrik Pedersen, with Dave Challinor coming in and winning his first two league games in charge.

Sheffield Wednesday are firmly in the automatic promotion hunt, let alone the play-off picture, following a 2-1 win away to South Yorkshire rivals Barnsley at Oakwell on Friday night. With other teams in the top half dropping points, they are well-placed to kick on.

Storch is currently recovering from back surgery, but he will be delighted that his first huge footballing decision has paid off already, with Storch reuniting Simon Wilson with Challinor in the process.

#2035. Exclusive: Swansea City & Burnley in race to sign Huddersfield Town star Joe Taylor

The January transfer window is just over a month away from opening, with EFL clubs already scouting new potential players ahead of the month-long chance to bolster their squads.

For clubs that have players that are starring in their leagues, they're going to face a fight to keep hold of them when it's all said and done, and then there are clubs at various points in the standings of any division that are going to look to strengthen their options.

And for high-flying Huddersfield Town in League One, they have a number of players who may be of interest to teams higher up in the footballing pyramid than they currently are - one player is certainly being looked at by Championship clubs.

Football League World has been exclusively informed that Terriers hot-shot Joe Taylor is a wanted man in the second tier ahead of the mid-season window.

Despite Dutch winger Derensili Sanches Fernandes taking most of the praise and plaudits for the West Yorkshire outfit since his summer arrival from Excelsior, Taylor has been quietly going about his business as part of their dangerous attacking unit, having forced his way back into contention at the Accu Stadium following his loan out to Wigan Athletic in 2025-26.

A look at the amount of pubs within a two-mile radius of every Championship ground this season.

The 24-year-old was shipped out temporarily by previous manager Lee Grant to the Latics, where he found his spark again, scoring 11 goals in half a season for them before returning to Town in the summer under new head coach Martin Drury.

Alongside the aforementioned Sanches Fernandes in a supporting attacking role, where the pair play behind more of a focal point such as Ashley Fletcher or Bojan Radulovic more often than not, Taylor has found the back of the net 10 times in League One already in just 14 outings, proving to be one of League One's best once again.

And that goalscoring performance is not going unnoticed, with FLW exclusively being able to reveal that managerless Swansea City, as well as struggling Burnley are both weighing up a move for the Welsh centre-forward in January.

Taylor has only sparringly played at Championship level before for Luton Town before getting his move to Huddersfield, but there are clubs looking at trying to get the attacker a move up the pyramid.

Swansea of course lost head coach Vitor Matos to Strasbourg last week, but it will not stop them eyeing up targets ahead of January, and Taylor is on their radar, even with a strike-force of Adam Idah, Ross Stewart and Zan Vipotnik to choose from - the latter was the Championship's top scorer last season but has failed to fire in 2026-27, and theoretically could be cashed in on to open up the space for another new forward.

Burnley meanwhile are in the Championship relegation zone and haven't won in Fabio Celestini's four matches in charge - they have centre-forward options like Jamie Vardy, Zeki Amdouni and Andreas Hountondji, but with a lack of goals coming from that particular trio, Taylor is being considered as a January option.

Whether Huddersfield would cash in on Taylor mid-season with their promotion aspirations remains to be seen, but given he's under contract until 2029, it'll likely take a significant amount of cash to prise him away from Drury's squad.

#2034. Charlie Austin tells Alex Neil to 'shut up' after Millwall v QPR comments

Former Queens Park Rangers goalscoring icon, Charlie Austin, has hit out at Millwall boss, Alex Neil, following the Scot's criticism towards Hoops winger, Paul Smyth, following Saturday's heated all-London affair at The Den.

Rangers continued their recently impressive form with a third victory in five matches by defeating the Lions 1-0 in SE16, courtesy of Nicolas Madsen's strike in the first minute of first-half stoppage time.

However, it is fair to say that the remainder of the contest wasn't without controversy, as the hosts were reduced to 10 men just 15 minutes into the contest after Zak Sturge's late challenge on the Northern Ireland international winger.

Although the statistics certainly showcased that Julien Stephan's side could have won the game by more if they finished their 31 attempts at Lukas Jensen's goal, much of Neil's post-match press conference centered around Smyth's involvement throughout.

The Saturday lunchtime victory saw Rangers end the Championship's 16th matchweek in seventh on 27 points, whilst Millwall sit 16th with nine fewer points.

Smyth, 29, is capable of featuring on either flank, and certainly caused plenty of issues for the Lions defence on Saturday in his 74-minute cameo, although Neil certainly had differing opinions.

“I spoke to Smyth about diving on the pitch in general. We had five players booked, and most of them came from him falling over," he said.

“The sending off – if he’s not offside, he’s not offside. If it’s a sending off, it’s a sending off. I’ve always been really straightforward with that sort of stuff. If it’s found that he’s guilty and he deserves to be sent off, I’m not going to argue that.

Neil was also booked for a verbal altercation with the Rs man, adding: “I told him to stop diving.

“I think what it was, it’s an element of frustration, but I’ve watched Paul Smyth for years. He’ll probably come up here and tell you he never dives, but I’d beg to differ.”

Austin is a former teammate of Smyth's at Loftus Road, having returned to W12 back in 2020, scoring 15 goals in 59 appearances during his second spell, which lasted for two seasons.

The 37-year-old now offers regular opinions on Championship developments, and he defended the 26-time international when asked on his YouTube channel to give a verdict on Sturge's dismissal.

"I'm going to say yes," he said. "Paul Smyth does well there. He gets his body in the way and knows what's coming.

"Alex Neil comes out and says he was diving all around the pitch. Shut up mate.

"You'd like to have Paul Smyth in your team," Austin stated.

"Seriously. The threat he gives when 'we' have the ball, but when 'we' haven't, he presses and uses his pace well. He entices defenders to get close to him, which brings a foul and he anticipates the touch is coming.

"But, for Alex Neil to come out and say that, I thought it was a stupid and naive comment."

The ex-Swindon Town frontman has offered his services after Ian Holloway was dismissed as manager

Austin knows exactly what it takes to achieve promotion to the Premier League, having done exactly that with the Hoops and West Bromwich Albion.

The former striker was certainly encouraged by Rangers' performance against their London rivals this weekend, especially the way in which they continued to impose themselves on the contest despite the hosts' desire to remain defensively solid.

Rangers and Millwall fans, do you agree with Alex Neil or Charlie Austin? Comment below!

Neil's comments, unsurprisingly, split opinion depending on which side of the fence those who watched the 90 minutes sat on, but that doesn't take away from the threat Smyth can possess, with the attacker already scoring and assisting three goals this campaign.

#2033. Is Mauricio Pochettino’s job at Manchester United the toughest in the Premier League?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United hired Mauricio Pochettino as their next manager to replace Michael Carrick, who managed just one win in 10 games.

His appointment makes him Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

Pochettino brings considerable Premier League experience after previous spells with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. He has also managed Paris Saint-Germain before the USA job.

As he faces Liverpool for his first game on Sunday, the question arises: is he facing the toughest job in the Premier League?

The question was posed on BBC Radio about who is going to have more pressure, Pochettino or Thomas Frank at Crystal Palace.

According to former Premier League defender Nedum Onuoha, the expectations surrounding Manchester United will make the Argentine’s job considerably harder.

Pochettino is preparing for his first game in charge of Manchester United, with Liverpool waiting at Anfield on November 22. However, the challenge facing the new manager goes beyond getting results on the pitch.

Onuoha believes Pochettino will have to deal with constant discussion and criticism about his work, much of it coming from former United players who are now in the media.

Choosing between Pochettino and Frank, Onuoha said, “Probably Pochettino, because every former Manchester United player works in the media, so there will always be discussion around what he is doing.

“Whereas Frank can just enjoy playing his football at Crystal Palace. If he does well then it is great, if he doesn’t do well then it is still OK.

“But from Pochettino’s perspective, if Manchester United finish the season 15th in the Premier League, whether we like it or not, there will be some criticism of him because he’s had 28 games to do something.”

The comments just highlight the difference in expectations at the two clubs. Frank may have more freedom to work without the same level of attention, while Pochettino will be judged from day one against the standards historically associated with Manchester United. That is one big problem for Pochettino.

Rory Smith from The Observer highlighted another glaring problem at United.  Highlighting a major problem, Smith said, “there is a cycle element to Manchester United whereby a manager comes in, makes things a bit better, and then within a year to 18 months they aren’t challenging for titles again because the Premier League has changed since they were a dominant force.”

Pochettino’s first taste of action as a United manager will be against Liverpool at Anfield on November 22. That opening fixture will give him an immediate test, but the bigger task will be to get back United to winning ways, step by step.

Will the Manchester United job be without pressure for Mauricio Pochettino? Absolutely Not.

#2032. Manchester United consider legal action over JJ Gabriel departure

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Manchester United are prepared to consider legal action if evidence emerges that another club approached academy forward JJ Gabriel without permission.

The 16-year-old announced his departure from Old Trafford in a social media video on Tuesday and is expected to join Real Madrid in January. According to The Times and ESPN, United remain concerned about the circumstances surrounding his proposed move, although no breach of transfer regulations has been established.

Gabriel has been absent from United since September, when he requested the cancellation of his registration. The teenager remains registered with the club, and United could explore legal or regulatory options if evidence of an unauthorised approach emerges.

The Independent reports that United do not want to punish Gabriel for actions they believe may have been taken by adults involved in his future. Real Madrid have been widely linked with the forward, but his transfer has not been formally completed.

Gabriel joined United’s academy in 2020 and was named the club’s young player of the year last season. He featured for the senior side during pre-season but has not made a competitive first-team appearance.

The youngster is eligible for a move within the European Union under an exception to FIFA’s rules on international transfers involving players aged under 18. In his farewell message, Gabriel thanked United for helping him develop during his six years at the club.

His expected move to Madrid would bring that association to an end, although questions remain over the process leading to his departure. United have not announced legal proceedings, and there has been no finding of wrongdoing by Real Madrid or any other club.

Manchester United have been linked with Como midfielder Nico Paz, although Real Madrid’s buy-back option and the absence of reported negotiations leave considerable uncertainty over a potential move.

The 22-year-old Argentina international has impressed in Italy this season, scoring six goals and providing eight assists in 14 appearances. According to The Sun, United have been monitoring Paz ahead of a possible summer transfer, with Mauricio Pochettino’s appointment potentially helping their chances.

Transfer journalist Fabrizio Romano has questioned the strength of United’s reported interest, saying there has been no contact or serious negotiation. Romano explained that the link had emerged because the same agency represents Paz and Pochettino.

He also suggested that Madrid remain central to the player’s future and that a January move is not being considered. United could assess their attacking midfield options next summer, with captain Bruno Fernandes’ contract situation still unresolved.

For now, Paz remains a reported target rather than a player involved in active transfer talks.

#2030. Chris Wilder snaps at reporter in Sheffield United press-conference after Sydie Peck question

With three wins in their last four matches, Sheffield United have found some form heading in to the busy December period.

And one of Chris Wilder's stars of the campaign has been Sydie Peck, who remained at Bramall Lane despite transfer attention from elsewhere, is operating on another level.

Peck went through the entire 2024-25 Championship season without scoring, but after notching five goals last season, he's already matched that tally from midfield in 16 outings in 2026-27 - adding three assists to that tally too.

Peck - who joined United from Arsenal's youth setup in 2021 - rarely plays together with fellow midfield youngster Oliver Arblaster, who came through the Blades academy, but they started alongside each other in the engine room in the 4-0 rout of Watford this past weekend.

That pairing has been a source of contention for many United supporters in recent times - Peck's run in the first-team on a regular basis only really began when Arblaster was sidelined with a knee injury two seasons ago, and the latter was left sidelined more often than not when he was fit and ready to return last year.

They worked pretty well together against an abject Hornets side, but Wilder seemed to object to a question posed to him about whether or not they can work as a good pairing on a regular basis.

Wilder seemed utterly bemused, noting they've only played together six times in midfield, winning three and losing two, and he believes that fans are waiting for Peck and Arblaster to 'fail' as a partnership for whatever reason - you can watch the full rant below.

Arblaster's emergence in Sheffield United's relegated Premier League team in 2024, following a stint on loan at Port Vale, was a genuinely exciting moment - despite the drop back to the Championship, United had a player that was ready to start week in, week out in the Championship.

Sadly, his knee injury set him back a year, but it allowed Peck to emerge from the shadows and become the player he has now developed into - whilst still a raw talent, there's a reason why Premier League clubs have been circling in recent times from the likes of Newcastle United and Sunderland.

Manchester City fan and former boxer Anthony Phythian has named English football's FIVE hardest hooligan firms

If Peck continues to seriously impress, then Sheffield United will have a big decision to make in the January window should bids arrive at their door - selling Andre Brooks, Callum O'Hare and Gus Hamer for decent money in the summer though could mean the club are in a stronger financial position than many think.

Every player has a price though, and with January fast approaching, there's a chance that the Peck and Arblaster partnership may not have that much time to flourish.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#2029. Lisandro Martinez to Barcelona: Deco gives verdict on the move for defender

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United signed Lisandro Martinez in 2022 from Ajax for £57 million but at the end of his contract, he might leave United for free.

Martinez is now in his fifth season at Old Trafford after joining from Ajax for £57 million in 2022. He has made 121 appearances in all competitions for the club, but his long-term future remains unclear.

Manchester United are not expected to stand in his way if a suitable opportunity to leave comes, especially following his public criticism of the club’s transfer strategy last month.

The defender is out of contract at the end of the season, although United have the option to trigger a further 12 months. Whether the club chooses to use that clause remains to be seen.

A departure from Manchester United could give Martinez the chance to find a new challenge after four seasons in Manchester. Barcelona had looked like a possible destination, but the latest reports suggest they are not currently pushing for his signature.

Lisandro Martinez’s hopes of joining Barcelona appear to have suffered a major setback, with reports from Spain claiming that neither sporting director Deco nor manager Hansi Flick is convinced by the Manchester United defender.

Atletico Madrid had also been mentioned among the interested clubs but there weren’t any further reports on a possible transfer, leaving Martínez’s options in Spain uncertain.

The latest claims suggest a switch to the Camp Nou may be unlikely.

Journalist Pedro Bravo on El Chiringuito reports that Martínez’s profile does not appeal to either member of Barcelona’s sporting leadership.

“Lisandro, as far as I’m aware, neither Deco nor Flick are keen on him,” Bravo was quoted as saying.

The journalist also claimed to have spoken directly with Deco, who is also ruled Martinez out.

“He’s a good player, but we don’t like him. He doesn’t fit in with us.”

❌ "LISANDRO MARTÍNEZ NO GUSTA a DECO ni FLICK".😱 El superagente @PedroBravoJ lo desvela en #ElChiringuitoEnEnergy. pic.twitter.com/Frt2KAG3q4

Lisandro Martinez is not expected to renew his current contract but would be expecting that United doesn’t trigger his one-year extension clause. With United not expected to sell him in the winter transfer window, United may be looking at extending his deal to recoup some transfer fees by selling him in the summer transfer window.

#2028. Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

It was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes showed he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

The one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward quickly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

Devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n

Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

You would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they showed to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

Top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA

Trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

Leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6

It was an entertaining affair, mercifully lacking the bile that would usually bubble away when it is staged in England, and the longer the game advanced, the better Leeds looked. They finished the opening period strongly and came back after the restart, with 10 changes, in the same fettle.

Farke, whose team had shown their ability to score heavily when they pummelled Liverpool 4-2 in Chicago 10 days ago, would have taken plenty of encouragement, but the perfectionist in him would have cursed the opportunities that were squandered early in the second period.

The misses proved costly as the game meandered and the shoot-out went United’s way, after Wilson and James Justin failed from 12 yards, with Noussair Mazraoui thumping in the decisive kick. It really is never dull.

Decent enough watch for roughly half the game, settled on a shoot-out in which Alex Cairns got nowhere near any of Manchester United’s penalties. Doubt he will lose much sleep over it. Bruno Fernandes grinned broadly when he missed.

Bottom left. Manchester United win the Boyle Sports Cup.

The ref decides to call time as the stewards cannot catch the juvenile intruders.

Some sealion ball juggling from Mazraoui involving foot, thigh and head, gets him past Justin on the right  but Gnonto heads away his cross.

Seven Manchester United changes: Mee, Tielmans, Shaw, Bruno Fernandes, Jack Fletcher, Matheus Cunha and Mazraoui incoming for Dalot, Lammens, Amass, Mbeumo, Diallo, Zirkzee and Tyler Fletcher.

The ref blows directly on 45 minutes moments after Nmecha rab out of room to control Tanaka’s cross and booted it out for a Man Utd goal-kick.

Manchester United probe patiently for half a minute around the Leeds area but the pass supposed to play Mbeumo through is picked off by Bijol and he plays it out to James who hares off down the left for 50 yards, cuts in on his right after leaving Yoro in his vapour trail, and whacks a shot over the bar from 22 yards.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester United and Leeds United at a sold-out Croke Park in Dublin. Last year Leeds played Milan in the Irish capital and drew a crowd of 52,000 but at the GAA citadel, as I think I’m contractually obliged to call it, there will be 83,000 present, a testament to the Premier League’s reach and these two clubs’ popularity in Ireland founded on the exploits of Billy Whelan, Noel Cantwell, Johnny Giles, Roy Keane, Gary Kelly et al. It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

It’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

This one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game. Leeds’ pre-season has gone well: after a 3-2 defeat by Wrexham in Tampa, they have beaten Sunderland in New Jersey, Liverpool in Chicago and RB Leipzig at Elland Road. Manchester United also lost to Wrexham (in Helsinki) then beat Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atlético in Stockholm and drew one apiece with the European champions, PSG, in Gothenburg last time out.

While Leeds will have new signing James Trafford available and Noah Okafor, who scored twice in Leeds’ first league victory at Old Trafford for 45 years last April, in the squad for the first time after the World Cup, Manchester United have Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in training since the start of the week but it seems too soon for them to start but Youri Tielemans is pushing to make his first start.

#2027. Who stays and who leaves Manchester United under Mauricio Pochettino, Gary Neville reveals list

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United hired Mauricio Pochettino as their next manager to replace Michael Carrick, who managed just one win in 10 games.

His appointment makes him Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

Pochettino takes charge of Manchester United sitting in an unfamiliar 18th in the Premier League table with only one win from 10 matches. He has a massive job ahead of him, with many pundits and former players terming his situation the toughest in the Premier League.

Gary Neville believes the Argentine will need several transfer windows to get the squad where he wants it, if he gets that much of time at Manchester United.

The former captain shared his views on which players he expects Pochettino to keep, and who could be heading for the exit.

Neville believes Senne Lammens should remain part of the plans, although he expects Pochettino to bring in another goalkeeper to give him some competition for his place. At the back, he backed Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire and Leny Yoro to stay, while suggesting Ayden Heaven needs a loan move to the Championship.

“Heaven, I’d loan him out, get some experience in the Championship. He’s nowhere near it, it’s unfair to put him in the situation he’s in,” Neville said on Stick to Football.

In midfield, Neville wants Pochettino to build around Bruno Fernandes, Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans. He also believes Andrey Santos could have a future at the club because of his age, mobility and aggression.

Mason Mount, however, is not part of his plans. Neville said: “Mount would have to go” and identified him as the player to leave from that midfield group.

Neville also has his doubts on the forward line, with much of the front line seeing a change. Gary Neville expects Joshua Zirkzee to leave and believes United cannot continue paying Marcus Rashford’s wages.

“Zirkzee definitely to go. I think Marcus 100 per cent to go because he’s on massive money and that story has been well told. They can’t afford to pay him that money, you have to get rid of that wage at the earliest opportunity.”

He expects Pochettino to work with Amad Diallo, Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and Benjamin Sesko. Patrick Dorgu could also be useful in the short term, although Neville thinks he may leave within the next couple of years. Manuel Ugarte, meanwhile, was another player he was certain would go.

Talking about the exits, Gary Neville has singled out many United stars to be shown the door in the first wave of squad clearance by Mauricio Pochettino. Neville identified Lisandro Martínez, Matthijs de Ligt and Noussair Mazraoui as further candidates to leave in the first wave of departures, alongside Mount, Rashford and Zirkzee.

Neville believes another group of exits could follow a year later, with Shaw, Maguire, Diogo Dalot and Fernandes among the players whose futures may not be at the club in long term. Pochettino would also have to decide whether Santos and Carlos Baleba fit into his long-term plans.

Neville does not expect United to rebuild the squad in a single summer, even if Pochettino makes a positive start.

“But the earliest Mauricio Pochettino can unravel this squad is two seasons if he does well. It could take three to get this squad unravelled.”

Pochettino’s first game comes against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday. His immediate priority will be to get some results for Manchester United but beyond the immediate games and results, Manchester United are expected to make multiple exits from the club as Pochettino settles into the job.

#2026. 5 players should follow Ernie Weaver out of Sheffield Wednesday in January

Sheffield Wednesday find themselves in a peculiar position regarding their academy, as a lot of young homegrown talents introduced themselves to the fanbase at Championship level last season due to "circumstances," but now need to find regular game time elsewhere.

That's the view of new Owls boss Dave Challinor, who has hinted that a few loan departures may be on the cards for some of the younger players in the squad who put themselves in the limelight during their difficult campaign last season under administration.

Wednesday's ability to build a squad over the past summer window has meant that, despite some fans looking forward to seeing these young players become the core of a new-look side, they've fallen by the wayside.

Challinor stated that Ernie Weaver, one of the early standouts from last season before being sidelined for the majority of the campaign with a foot injury, could be someone who leaves on a short-term deal in January, following the likes of Charlie McNeill, Cole McGhee and Reece Johnson, who all played some part in the Championship last season.

These five players should also be tipped for a loan move in the near future to get some valuable game time, too.

Dave Challinor namedropped a couple of other players who could leave the club on loan at some point in the near future. One of those was fellow centre-back Gabriel Otegbayo.

The Irish Under-21 international epitomised the chances that young players got last season while the club was in administration. The former Burnley academy man made 35 Championship appearances last season, including a run of 23 starts in the final 25 games.

Otegbayo began this season as one of the first-choice defenders under Henrik Pedersen, too, starting four of the first five in league action and scoring in his one appearance off the bench against Bromley in that 7-2 demolition.

Since that fifth game, though, the 21-year-old hasn't started in the league, and he's to feature in a matchday squad in League One under Challinor. Indeed, his only appearance under the new boss came in the 4-0 EFL Trophy defeat against Accrington Stanley.

Wednesday fans weren't too enamoured with his performances in the early stages of the season, and also feel that he could benefit from a spell elsewhere.

The other player mentioned by Challinor as a potential loan option was midfielder Jarvis Thornton, who signed a new two-year deal with the Owls this past summer.

The 20-year-old has been at Wednesday since he was eight years old and was one of the many academy graduates who made their first-team debuts last season. He was one of the main features of their run to the EFL Cup third round, and he made 23 league appearances, too.

This season, though, Thornton has been one of the main victims of the midfield being strengthened at Hillsborough. The returns of Barry Bannan and Jaiden Heskey, plus the addition of Billy Mitchell, have made it difficult for him to get minutes.

His last league appearance came in that 7-2 win over Bromley nearly three months ago, and he's made a matchday squad just once since then.

The new contract ensures that the decision-makers at Wednesday think he has a bright future, but he may need to begin to realise that elsewhere.

It was a proud moment for Sean Fusire against Accrington Stanley in the EFL Trophy, as he wore the captain's armband for the first time. Unfortunately, the Zimbabwe international hasn't been able to stake a claim for regular league minutes this season, though.

The 21-year-old, unlike the others on this list so far, has actually spent time out on loan from Sheffield Wednesday. He spent the second half of the 2024/25 campaign at Carlisle United in League Two, but was then thrust into Championship action last year.

Which fanbases can improve on their current atmosphere offerings? The computer has had its say....

Only seven players played more league minutes than Fusire last season, but the full-back only has a couple in League One this year, coming on for the final stages of Henrik Pedersen's final game in charge at Doncaster Rovers.

Under Challinor, he has appearances in cup competitions, but hasn't made a league squad yet. You feel that, once the January window opens, he'll be one of the first out the door.

It was a pleasant surprise for Wednesday fans to see George Brown starting against Accrington Stanley. It was the 20-year-old's first appearance in nearly 11 months after a season plagued by injury.

Like Weaver, it was a real frustration to see him sidelined during the campaign in which he'd have gotten exposure at Championship level. He scored twice in just seven second-tier games last year, including one of their two wins all year at Portsmouth, and looked very promising.

He needs game time, but he won't get it at Hillsborough anytime soon. A good loan move away, perhaps at the top of the National League, could be massively beneficial to his chances of making it back in the senior fold in South Yorkshire.

There arguably isn't a more exciting talent on Sheffield Wednesday's books right now than Will Grainger. The Welsh Under-19 international only just turned 18 earlier this month, and broke through towards the end of last season, scoring in a 4-1 defeat against Oxford United.

He also extended his contract with the Owls over the summer, but he, too, has been a victim of the strengthening of the squad, especially across the frontline.

Do you think Will Grainger will be a major player in Sheffield Wednesday's bid to rise back up the EFL? Let us know in the comments.

Wednesday won't just be wanting to loan him out to any club for minutes; they'll be taking great care with this decision, as the 18-year-old could be a cornerstone of this new era under the Arise ownership.

A good League Two move could work wonders for Grainger and put him in brilliant standing to properly break into the Owls' senior side next season, if they remain in League One.

#2023. Birmingham City must offload rarely-seen star who Wayne Rooney called a 'top player'

Birmingham City's recent progress has led to a strong amount of player turnover at St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park, and now there is a strong focus on what could be in store come the opening of the January transfer window.

It has been made no secret that Chris Davies' side are looking to reach the Premier League in the near future, with the 41-year-old receiving plenty of backing from Knighthead Capital Management during a near two-and-a-half-year tenure.

Birmingham's strong start to the Championship season followed an intriguing summer transfer window, but they were swiftly knocked off the division's summit last weekend after a lacklustre defeat to fellow promotion hopefuls, Stoke City, on Saturday.

It was an encounter in which plenty of issues which came to a head last season for Blues were evident, including a lack of urgency in attacking areas. As such, the debate has continued as to which areas need strengthening within Davies' squad with the January window looming large.

On top of such decisions, it feels inevitable that some of those within the Blues ranks may move on to new pastures, including rather luckless full-back, Lee Buchanan.

Buchanan's senior career began seven years ago, earning a first-team berth with Derby County under Phillip Cocu for the 2019/20 campaign.

It wasn't until the 2020/21 campaign, which saw the Rams narrowly escape relegation under the management of Wayne Rooney, where the full-back earned his major breakthrough with 37 appearances, being named the club's Young Player of the Season in the process.

During the early weeks of that particular season, Buchanan was called up to the England Under-20s squad, where he revealed that Rooney, who became his Birmingham boss just under three years later, predicted a bright future in the game for the defender.

“He’s England’s all-time top scorer so speaking to him obviously helps a lot," said Buchanan.

“He told me to go out there and enjoy myself, to keep doing what I do for the club and that he’s sure I’d be fine."

The 2021/22 season was a difficult campaign for Derby, although Buchanan was one of several academy graduates to emerge with credit for his performance levels at Pride Park which would have resulted in Championship survival, were it not for a 21-point deduction.

The defender was then the subject of a controversial departure to Bundesliga side, Werder Bremen, where he would link up with current Birmingham teammate, Marvin Ducksch, for the first time, making 21 appearances in the German top-flight before swiftly returning to the Midlands under current Rams head coach, John Eustace.

At 22 years of age, Blues certainly invested in Buchanan's potential in their first transfer window of the Knighthead era, with the left-back penning a five-year deal.

Blues are looking for supporters to help shape the outlook of the club's future home

Three of those have now passed, and the defender's time in B9 has become one to forget, not least due to an unfortunate ACL injury which kept him sidelined between December 2024 and August 2026.

Buchanan has only played 40 times for Birmingham since his arrival in July 2023, with the bulk of said appearances coming during the club's relegation campaign of 2023/24, prior to Alex Cochrane's arrival.

Davies opted to select Buchanan during pre-season and in the 1-0 win over Swansea City in the EFL Cup first round following his recovery with the Blues boss saying: “I looked at him before the game and thought if he’s called upon he's ready to go now and it says a lot for the man, as well as the player.”

Whilst Buchanan's character has never been doubted, his long-term position at St. Andrew's is far from secure, and that was certainly the case in the summer window.

In January, Davies was in no rush to loan out the defender despite Kai Wagner arriving as back-up to Cochrane, and even though the German swiftly returned to Philadelphia Union, Buchanan also attracted transfer interest.

League One promotion hopefuls, Luton Town and Reading, were credited with interest, but, ultimately, a move failed to materialise.

At 25 years of age, Buchanan is set to be entering the prime of his career, and the chances of reigniting his career seem very little at Birmingham right now.

Cochrane has continued as Davies' mainstay following the exit of Wagner, and whilst Kristoffer Lund has also suffered injury misfortune this season, the seven-time USMNT international does appear to be ahead of Buchanan in the pecking order.

Blues fans, could Lee Buchanan have become a key figure at St. Andrew's without his injury woes? Comment below!

In January, there will be 18 months left on the full-back's contract, making it a prime opportunity for Blues to recoup some form of cash on his services, whilst allowing the player to rediscover form and match sharpness after just one competitive appearance 23 months.

#2022. What did the secret drone footage reveal about Manchester United training?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session was secretly filmed by a drone operator, who has since apologised and removed the footage from his YouTube channel after admitting his actions were unethical.

The footage showed players split into smaller groups carrying out different drills. On a separate full-size pitch, 11 players were positioned across the field alongside mannequins before gathering to receive instructions and feedback from new head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

Ten players were seen working with Pochettino in the video but only Harry Maguire, Kobbie Mainoo, Amad Diallo, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo are regular starters among those.

Another group involved in drills was that of Lisandro Martinez, Matthijs de Ligt, Youri Tielemans, Mason Mount, Leny Yoro, Noussair Mazraoui and Diogo Dalot.

In his statement, the operator said the flight itself was legal under drone regulations but accepted that recording the training session was wrong.

He explained that his intention was to give Manchester United supporters their first look at Pochettino wearing the club’s training kit.

He said: “A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part.”

The operator apologized directly to the club, its new head coach and the players.

“I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match.”

He also rejected any suggestion that Liverpool or another football club had been involved in his decision to film at Carrington.

“The video has been removed from my channel,” he added.

#2021. Jamie Carragher questions Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United appointment

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Jamie Carragher believes Mauricio Pochettino has as much to prove as Manchester United, suggesting the Argentine’s reputation is not fully backed up by his achievements.

Mauricio Pochettino is preparing for his first match in charge of Manchester United against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, following his departure from the United States national team to replace Michael Carrick.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager has arrived at Old Trafford with plenty of experience, but Carragher believes his appointment represents an opportunity for both United and Pochettino to rebuild their reputations.

Writing in The Telegraph, the former Liverpool defender highlighted the irony of United turning to a manager whose own career needs a fresh start.

“It is ironic that in their latest attempt to rejuvenate and restore some of their old fire, Manchester United have turned to a manager whose career needs a similar reawakening,” Carragher wrote.

He suggested that Pochettino should be grateful that a club of United’s stature came calling at this stage of his career.

“Manchester United need a savior to first ease them from the relegation zone and then revive their Premier League and Champions League credibility. Pochettino, meanwhile, needed a club like United to save him from a managerial career that promised more than it delivered.”

Manchester United were fortunate to secure a manager with Pochettino’s experience after dismissing Michael Carrick so early in the season. However, he believes the Argentine has plenty to prove despite his strong reputation in the game.

“The South American returns to England with a big reputation, but not enough on his CV to back up glowing testimonials,” he continued.

Carrick believes one of the biggest concerns surrounding Pochettino is his record in important matches.

“A recurring issue with Pochettino, which continued with the US team, is an inability to get over the line in the most consequential, winnable matches, resulting in a lack of big trophies.”

Despite questioning his ability to bottle in big games, he praised his teams when everything comes in together.

“Ten years ago his best team were the embodiment of him, full of energy, style and ambition. Time will tell whether this version of Pochettino is the one turning up at Old Trafford.”

Pochettino will have the chance to shut Carragher’s doubts on Sunday when Manchester United face Liverpool. His immediate priority will be to take United out of the relegation zone, but the expectations at Old Trafford will extend far beyond survival.

The Liverpool fixture will be his first opportunity to make an impression. Carragher, however, believes the Argentine’s real challenge is to turn his reputation into success.

Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has confirmed the club are discussing a new contract with Bruno Fernandes, but has refused to reveal any details about the negotiations as the midfielder approaches the final months of his current deal.

Fernandes’ contract expires at the end of the season, leaving Manchester United with an important decision to make over the future of their captain.

Speaking to Sky Sports, Berrada praised the Portuguese international for his contribution to the club and made clear how highly he is valued at Old Trafford.

#2018. 9 players set to miss Stoke vs Millwall

Stoke City could have the chance to go to the top of the Championship on Wednesday night, depending on how results on Tuesday go, when they host Millwall and former boss Alex Neil at the bet365 Stadium.

Stoke have continued their scintillating run of form under Mark Robins with a 1-0 home victory over Birmingham City at the weekend, leapfrogging the Blues in the Championship table, and now sit only behind Middlesbrough on goal difference as things stand.

Depending on how Boro get on against Swansea City on Tuesday night, Stoke could go to the top of the league with another three points in this fixture, though returning boss Neil is bound to make it as difficult as possible for the Potters.

Millwall haven't been at their best as of late, with just one win in their last seven league games, but with just two defeats in their last 16 games against Stoke, they have more often than not had the upper hand in this encounter in recent memory.

For Stoke, Djibril Soumare and George Hirst picked up minor knocks against Birmingham and will need to be assessed; Ethan Galbraith could come back into the side after illness, whilst Millwall wait on decisions on Luke Cundle, Josh Coburn, and Romain Esse, as Football League World takes a look at each player set to miss Wednesday's clash in the Potteries.

French striker Lamine Cisse has shown sparks of his talent this campaign, particularly in the games against Bolton Wanderers and Watford, but has been out of action since being forced off in Stoke's goalless draw with Bristol City a month ago.

It has since been confirmed that the 23-year-old will likely be out of action until Christmas, providing George Hirst, Robert Bozenik, and Sam Gallagher with chances to impress Robins up top.

Veteran full-back Aaron Cresswell has yet to make an appearance this season after extending his stay in North Staffordshire for another year over the summer, having picked up an injury during pre-season.

Robins confirmed that the 36-year-old was back on the grass training last month, but he still remains some way short of fitness, and isn't expected to make a return to the pitch just yet.

Football League World has asked AI to predict the 2027/28 EFL Championship table if Manchester United and Manchester City were in it

Luca Bombino has found minutes at left wing-back recently following an injury to Eric Bocat and impressed, with the American looking to make his mark in the Championship following his potential $5 million (£3.7 million) move from MLS side San Diego late in the summer window.

After picking up a yellow card in the first half against Birmingham, Bombino mistimed his challenge around the hour mark on Patrick Roberts, receiving his marching orders, and as a result, will be suspended for this game, as Bocat or Justin Devenny will likely take his place on the left flank for the Potters against Millwall.

Ato Ampah has endured a torrid time with injuries ever since joining Stoke from Chelsea's academy for a potential £3 million in January 2026, with the young winger still yet to make a senior appearance for the Potters nearly a year later.

The England youth international was on the cusp of a first-team return in October before a further injury setback means he will have to wait even longer for his Potters debut, as the youngster will be praying 2027 is his year.

Onto Millwall now, as left-back Zak Sturge is set to miss the trip to North Staffordshire after receiving an early red card in his side's narrow 1-0 home defeat to Queens Park Rangers at the weekend.

This means Alfie Doughty could come back into the fold to face his former side on Wednesday, or Jordi Osei-Tutu could be preferred in that role.

Mathis Servais joined Millwall in the summer from Belgian outfit KV Mechelen to much excitement, but with just nine minutes of Championship football to shout about nearly six months later, it hasn't exactly been the dream start to life at The Den he would've hoped for.

A hamstring injury in pre-season forced him to wait to make his debut, and another injury sustained in the following international break has kept him out of action since, and it doesn't look like he will be ready for this one.

Arguably the biggest absence for Millwall is French defender Tristan Crama, who, after an incredible full debut year for the Lions, has struggled with injury woes this campaign.

The 25-year-old has been limited to just five appearances so far this season, injuring both of his ankles, and has been absent from the side since Halloween's 4-1 victory over Derby County, where he was forced to come off just after the hour mark.

Filip Marschall joined Millwall in the summer from League One Stevenage to provide an alternative option between the sticks to Lukas Jensen and Max Crocombe, but after four appearances, he suffered ankle ligament damage against Lincoln City.

Jensen has since returned to the side and is expected to start between the sticks as the former Aston Villa youth player recovers.

#2017. Liverpool vs Man Utd: Preview, key stats, team news & where to watch

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Mauricio Pochettino begins his Manchester United reign with a huge test at Anfield on Sunday, with Manchester United desperate for a result after making their worst start to a top-flight season in 40 years.

Manchester United have collected just eight points from their opening 10 Premier League matches, with one win and five draws leaving them 18th in the table. They have also conceded in every league game this season and are currently on a run of 11 consecutive matches without keeping a clean sheet in all competitions.

Mauricio Pochettino only arrived to the club on Wednesday after replacing Michael Carrick, leaving him with just a few training sessions to prepare for one of the biggest fixtures in English football.

There is some encouragement for the Argentine, however. Eight of United’s last nine permanent or caretaker managers have avoided defeat in their first match in charge. That may be some encouragement to the Argentine.

Meanwhile, Liverpool are not exactly enjoying a comfortable season at home either. They sit fourth with 18 points but have won just once in their five Premier League matches at Anfield so far, giving them the third-worst home record in the Premier League.

Their recent form across all competitions stands at three wins, one draw and two defeats in their last six matches. Liverpool most recently beat Crystal Palace 3-1, but they will know that United’s poor league position does not make this fixture any less complicated.

Liverpool have received positive news ahead of Sunday’s meeting. Dominik Szoboszlai and Virgil van Dijk are both expected to feature, while Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong could also be available.

Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni have returned to team training following knee injuries but are unlikely to make the squad. Hugo Ekitike remains a long-term absentee with an Achilles problem.

Manchester United could welcome back Patrick Dorgu and Harry Maguire after both trained following fitness concerns. They were seen in that leaked drone footage as well. Lisandro Martínez is also available again after serving his suspension.

Luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford could return, although their availability remains uncertain. Carlos Baleba, Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko are still sidelined.

The new United boss has a difficult personal record against Liverpool. Pochettino has faced the Reds 19 times, winning three, drawing five and losing 11. He has also failed to win any of his last eight meetings with them in all competitions. That might be a concern, but everything has a first time.

Pochettino will be encouraged by United’s overall record against Liverpool.  United have an edge with 85 wins compared to Liverpool’s 72 across 218 meetings. Their most recent encounter also went their way, with a 3-2 victory on May 3.

However, United arrive on a disappointing run of seven consecutive away matches without a win and have managed just one victory in their last 11 games.
