#1948. Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City

Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the new signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

Title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

First Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N

Another notable incident was Martin Odegaard, not long after he had glossed a fabulous display with a third goal, sprinting 30 yards to spook Gianluigi Donnarumma and make the Italian hurry his clearance. The victory was good, the trophy was nice, but the energy heartened Arteta more than anything.

“They are really good examples,” Arteta said. “The way the team tracks back is unbelievable, especially when, fitness-wise, we aren’t there yet. We had desire and composure on the ball. When you put your soul and your heart into every action, this is what happens. We want to do it again.

“The desire comes from them thinking: ‘I want to live that moment again. I want to have all the moments again and I want them to be even bigger.’ We know what it is going to take. We have never done it [retain the Premier League] at this football club. We know it will demand something special.”

You could flip that and say it will take something special from the chasers. George Graham and Arsène Wenger could never hold on to the biggest prize during their reigns and you must return to Herbert Chapman, in Arsenal’s thriving 1930s, to find the only manager who went back-to-back.

It can feel premature (and can be foolish) to go out on a limb before the first weekend, but there was just something about them that felt different. Often in the past they have been overtly tentative when playing City, but they came out of their corner this time swinging – and they landed.

Enzo Maresca revealed afterwards that he “really didn’t like” how Arsenal had scored their first goal and that was putting it mildly, as there were 10 passes – broken only by the ball bouncing off Elliott Anderson’s shins – before Myles Lewis-Skelly ushered Calafiori into wreak havoc.

You had to go back to 1968, when City played West Brom, to find the last first-minute goal – City’s Bobby Owen was the scorer that day – and how Calafiori enjoyed it, shaking his fist in delight as Arsenal’s noisy fans reminded everyone of their status.

Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs

Here was a rude awakening for Anderson, City’s new £116m man. He was ever so slightly off the pace and that allowed Lewis-Skelly to slip a beautiful ball in behind the FA Cup winners’ defence and invite Calafiori to do the rest, which he did with assurance.

When Maresca watches back the video, he will see Abdukodir Khusanov sleeping and Phil Foden failing to press, but that should not detract from the quality of Arsenal’s interchanging – and it should also make whoever is hawking Lewis-Skelly around to clubs to think again. Why would he leave this?

It should not have been the case that a goal so soon should have governed how the game progressed, but that is exactly what happened as Arsenal completely dominated. Whenever they lost possession, they recovered it as a matter of urgency. Without Pep Guardiola on the touchline, City were like Samson after Delilah shaved his hair, devoid of all power.

City, in contrast to their opponents, showed a complete lack of desire and the second goal arrived when Odegaard was allowed time to flip a ball to the back post, where new boy Tzolis was arriving. The Greek headed back into the six-yard area and Kai Havertz did the rest.

Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F

Arsenal were criticised – fairly – during their title-winning campaign for being too physical and relying on gamesmanship, but if Havertz and Odegaard can stay fit for a prolonged period, the difference in style will be like night and day.

Throw in Tzolis, who was tricky and dynamic in Cardiff, to the mix and there will be another enhancement. He looks considerably better than Gabriel Martinelli, with more end product, and Bukayo Saka will do more down the right than Noni Madueke, who started here.

Maresca knew, with his team lacking fitness, that it would be difficult to overhaul the deficit once they had gone two goals behind but, really, he was lucky that Arsenal did not administer a genuine hiding which, at one stage, seemed as though they might.

Goal number three arrived just after the interval, again Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis were involved, combining to enable Odegaard to waltz into the area, hoodwinking Donnarumma so he sat down before sliding a contemptuous finish beyond him.

Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D

Had they gone through the gears, there could have been more, but it didn’t matter. What Arsenal showed was far more significant than a couple of more goals when the game was being disrupted by substitutions. The tackles, the running, energy and commitment – that is what brought Arteta joy.

“I’m extremely happy with the performance, the result and winning the first trophy,” Arteta purred.

You would be brave to say it will be their last.

Arsenal (4-2-3-1) Raya 7; White 7, Mosquera 7, Gabriel 7, Calafiori 7 (Hincapie h-t): Guimarães 7 (Rice h-t), Lewis-Skelly 8 (Zublimendi 75); Madueke 6 [Saka 60], Odegaard 8 (Eze 84), Tzolis 7; Havertz 7 (Gyokeres 75). Booked Calafiori, Odegaard. Subs Kepa (g), Merino, Dowman.

Goals: Calafiori (1), Havertz (28), Odegaard (48).

Manchester City (4-2-3-1) Donnarumma 5; Khusnaov 5, Dias 5, Gvardiol 5, O’Reilly 5; Anderson 5 (Lewis 60), Kovacic 5 (Gonzalez 79); Semenyo 6, Foden 5 (Cherki 60), Doku 6 (Grealish h-t); Haaland 5 (Marmoush 53). Booked Gvardiol, Foden. Subs Ait-Nouri, Reis, Nunes, Rulli (g).

It’s really sad. I’ve been fighting with the Premier League to extend & accommodate more players in the squad. They deserve to be in the squad, so hopefully we can change that rule.

I think the goal we conceded after 25 seconds unfortunately affected the game in that moment. I think after the goal, the reaction was quite good before they scored the second one, we had three or four chances to score and draw the game but unfortunately we conceded the second one and it became more complicated.

A really, really good performance so early in the season. To play at the level we did and the desire we showed, I just told them that I really enjoyed watching them.

He makes good decisions when a lot of people rush things, he did it twice in tight areas and two goals.

I joined midway [in pre-season]. This is the third game since I have been back. The feeling has been good. Today is frustrating, and it is a final that we all wanted to win. If there is a lesson to be learnt in the final, let it be this one, as there’s a lot more coming. It is a positive energy.

The feeling of a lot of work to put into. It’s part of any transition for things to be not so perfect in the beginning. You need to push through, you need to communicate, and make things work between us. I feel we’re in a very good way, but we need to keep on working. There’s going to be lots of challenges along the way.

Appears to the Community Shield trophy, which caught him a glancing blow to the face.

Trophy lift gone wrong, featuring Declan Rice 😂🏆📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ghmGZJDxka

The players judge the correct level of celebration judiciously, but then Mikel Merino cracks and starts spraying the champagne. While it is a semi-competitive game, Arteta and his players will point out that they earned their place in the fixture by winning the league.

Arsenal start the season with silverware 🏆The Community Shield belongs to the Gunners!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M6GqsGkRF7

What happens to them? I’m not sure the winners’ medals would take pride of place, let alone the silvers.

We played some brilliant football. Great performance and a great way to start the season.

I always want to help the team as much possible with goals and assists. I want to score more goals.

We showed our level today. We’re showed we’re ready. We’re serious and we want to do it again.

We want to attack it. We want to do it again. When you get a taste of how nice it is you want to do it again.

The league champions kick-off the domestic season with a resounding and stylish victory. Shades of 1998 and 2004 when they swept Manchester United aside in this fixture as title winners, only to fail to defend the crown in the season that followed. So maybe it is unwise to make bold forecasts, but it could not have gone better for Arteta. Odegaard, Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis caught the eye, and Arsenal had their usual solidarity defensively. City just completely off the pace, one to write off and move on.

Marmoush is feeling his hip after a challenge by Mosquera. City have a free-kick wide right. Gabriel heads away Grealish’s delivery in trademark fashion.

Just three minutes of added time to play. No City player is there to meet Cherki’s low cross and White can clear under little pressure.

Rice uncharacteristically caught dallying in midfield but City cannot capitalise. Cheers from the Arsenal fans as Saka wins a throw in from Grealish. Marmoush with a chance to run at Mosquera, but his touch is far too heavy.

City have a free-kick in a crossing position right of centre, but many of their fans are now packing up their banners and heading for the exits. If they haven’t already. Cherki’s delivery is poor, and Rice heads away.

Odegaard with a loose touch, and a yellow card for catching Grealish with the resulting challenge. That was the Arsenal captain’s last action of the game, he is replaced by Eberechi Eze. Odegaard has looked back to his 2024 past today, Eze’s best chance of a start might be from the left.

City’s best move of the second half: Cherki gliding through the challenges and finding Semenyo with a lovely reverse pass, and his shot was drilled towards the far corner. Sharp reflexes by Raya to plunge to his right and save.

Nico Gonzalez replaces Kovacic as Maresca makes his sixth change of the second half. The game has felt like a training exercise since Odegaard’s third goal with the occasional flash of quality.

Chance for Saka! Cracking low cross from Hincapie, but Saka sweeps over from near the penalty spot. Too much on it as he tried to help the ball on its way.

Better tempo to Manchester City’s football, and Gvardiol has gone down holding his face in the box. It was more of a shoulder to shoulder with White, and the incident is checked and cleared by VAR.

Here come two more Arsenal changes: Havertz and Lewis-Skelly deserve their ovation, replaced by Gyokeres and Zubimendi.

Chance for Tzolis to play Saka clean through on goal but he delayed a fraction and Gvardiol got back in to defend. It was a great flick on by Havertz to free Tzolis. Gyokeres is ready to replace the German.

Cherki with a shot from distance, saved by Raya. That was City’s first shot on target of the second half.

Odegaard with a disguised ball through to White, who may have been offside, and Tzolis is close to applying the touch that would have made it four. Feels like the game is meandering towards its conclusion.

Arsenal back themselves to play out from a tight spot again, but Semenyo does well to force Hincapie to concede a throw in. Arsenal then soak up another spell of City possession, they have been so much more compact defensively than Maresca’s team. Whenever Arsenal have the ball in City’s half they look dangerous, whereas City’s possession has been sterile.

City chasing shadows when Arsenal play out from the back. Arsenal moving the ball with great assurance, but you suspect everyone has an extra yard of space than they would find in a full-throttle Premier League game.

Semenyo gave Hincapie a tough time in the League Cup final in March, and was not shy in boasting about it after the game. I suspect Hincapie is a defender who keeps a little black book of those who have crossed him.

Lovely moment in midfield from Odegaard, letting the ball run across his box and pushing it beyond Rico Lewis. Saka in acres on the far side after he outmuscles Gvardiol, but he shoots into the side netting. Tried to give Donnarumma the eyes.

City with a spell of possession in the Arsenal half, and Gvardiol glances a header over the bar from a very decent Grealish cross. Arsenal hard to break down once they are in that 4-4-2 shape.

Here come the changes: Foden and Anderson off, Cherki and Rico Lewis on.

Arsenal subs: Saka and Hincapue on for Calafiori and Madueke. Saka has braids this seasons, so a new look.

Arsenal popping the ball around in the sunshine now, to olés from their fans. Maresca is about to make two more changes, so five subs before the hour tells you were City are physically. Saka is going to come on for Arsenal.

Gvardiol booked, and here come more City changes, this is a fitness exercise for Maresca now. Haaland and O’Reilly off, Marmoush and Guehi on. Arteta will surely reply in kind around the hour mark.

That really should be game over now, but given the loosey-goosey nature of these games I suppose you never know. I think the only way this fixture can matter is if one team takes a battering, and there’s a risk of that for City now.

Christos Tzolis registered 29 assists in 52 competitive games for Club Brugge last season. He’s on two assists in 48 competitive minutes for Arsenal.

What composure from the Arsenal captain, running into the box untracked and sitting down first Gvardiol then Donnarumma before finding the empty net. It is clever play from Tzolis, finding Odegaard with the pass for his second assist of the game. The run from Calafiori was important to pull City’s defence out of shape.

Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D

Man City kick off in the second 45 minutes. These matches tend to lose their rhythm in the second half.

So far, Manchester City’s first glimpse of life after Pep Guardiola is inauspicious. Enzo Maresca might be his predecessor’s doppelgänger, but his attempt to emulate the same style has proved abortive: plenty of possession, but minimal impact. It smacks of desperation that Jack Grealish is being thrown in at half-time, his first appearance for the club for 15 months.

Looks like a pre-planned change from Manchester City and Arsenal: Jack Grealish makes an unlikely comeback, replacing Doku, and Declan Rice replaces Bruno Guimaraes. Arsenal’s two big hitters in midfield sharing the game.

7 - Kai Havertz has been involved in more goals against Manchester City (7 - 4 goals, 3 assists) than against any other side in his club career. Occasion. pic.twitter.com/ln7PQnjboJ

00:23 - Riccardo Calafiori's goal for Arsenal after 23 seconds is the first scored in the opening minute of the Community Shield since Bobby Owen for Manchester City against West Bromwich Albion in 1968.Rapid. pic.twitter.com/FCwVKuTOlh

Advantage Arsenal at half time, and they have looked a sharper, more cohesive team. City have had plenty of possession, but much of it was sterile until that late flurry when Raya saved from Haaland and White blocked Doku’s shot. The first 45 minutes will have ticked all of the boxes for Arteta: there has been some strong penalty box defending, some flowing moves from back to front and two well-taken goals.

Flimsy defending from City again, Havertz finding it easy to run to the byline, and the ball is cleared off the line after Odegaard poked the ball towards goal after a Donnarumma parry.

“You’re getting sacked in the morning,” sing the Arsenal fans at Maresca as the whistle blows.

Mosquera defends well against Doku at the expense of a corner, which Raya claims with ease. There is going to be just one minute of added time.

Arsenal playing through the pitch and City’s defensive shape again, this time it was started by a fizzed Raya pass into Tzolis. Three on three, but Madueke’s shot is straight at Donnarummma. The winger is such an outlet for his team, but the final decision is lacking too often, which is not a novel observation.

Madueke then finds White on the overlap, he chips the ball to the back post where Calafiori is free and he volleys over.

Arsenal’s defence stretched for the first time in the game. Raya saved after Haaland was picked out by Doku, with Lewis-Skelly defending well to deny a rebound, before Semenyo picks out Doku with a lofted cross, but White through himself in front of the volley and made a crucial block.

Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N

Madueke with a tame shot on goal after O’Reilly went Awol defensively, but the flag was up for offside.

Arsenal come forward again, with Havertz holding the ball up well. Tzolis reverses a pass for Calafiori, but he anticipates a challenge in the area and is rightly booked for diving.

Ben White thought he had nipped in front of Doku to intercept a straight Kovacic pass, but the referee blows for a foul against the Arsenal man.

Then Haaland has a sight of goal for the first time: a peeling run into the right channel, found by Doku, but it was tough angle on his weaker foot. Scooped it over the bar.

Foden takes up a lovely position behind the Arsenal midfield, but his through ball towards Haaland hits Gabriel on the back of the heel. Then Semenyo wins a corner in a joust with Calafiori. Referee blows for some pushing and shoving.

Eventually the corner is taken, cleared initially, before teasing Foden cross drifts beyond the back post. Foden the pick of the bunch for City, which is unsurprising considering he has a full pre-season behind him.

The Arsenal supporters are really, really enjoying this. They’re “doing the Poznan” to mock the City fans.

An ideal outing for Arsenal, so far though it can be easy to over-index these games when players are not fully match fit. But Arteta will be pleased with the fluency in the passing through midfield, which was lacking at times last season.

Christos Tzolis was signed to provide goals and assists, and he’s been doing so throughout pre-season. The Greek winger is perhaps more aggressive in his positioning than Leandro Trossard, the man he has replaced in the squad, and he was in the right place there to pick out Kai Havertz.

The new signing Tzolis is involved with a clever header back across the six-yard box, the left winger was picked out by an inswinging Odegaard cross to the back post. Havertz rose above Dias, and his header down into the turf squeezed beyond Donnarumma. The ball bounced in off the back of the goalkeeper, could well be an own goal.

Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F

Gvardiol slides across to win an important challenge when Madueke was running into space, before Odegaard fails with a scooped pass towards White.

Arsenal find Madueke in acres of space again, Bruno Guimaraes with the switch, and the winger keeps things alive despite an unconvincing dribble. Guimaraes then finds space in the box, but takes to long to pick out a man.

City soon on the attack again, and Doku runs off the back of White all too easily, but Gabriel charges in to win a booming slide tackle in the box. He greets it with his own roar of approval.

Raya claims the corner, then Foden is booked for pulling back Tzolis to stop a counter.

In these early days, long before trophies become something tangible, Mikel Arteta will want to see something far more vital than talent - hunger. It’s bursting out of Arsenal’s players, never more apparent than when Gabriel has just thundered into Jeremy Doku and celebrated the challenge like a goal. It reflective of the team’s mentality.

The passion from Gabriel after stopping Jérémy Doku 😤📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/L3D8lHrBNU

City’s best moment so far: Foden with a shot from just outside the box which is pushed clear by Raya, before O’Reilly is penalised for a push on Ben White. It looked like the City man was just stronger in the shoulder to shoulder. Perhaps out frustration, O’Reilly then fouls Havertz on halfway.

The Arsenal fans massively outnumber the City supporters here, and the Londoners appear to have fallen in love with Guimaraes already. He’s snapping into tackles with real venom. There have been lots of cries of “Bruno!” in these opening 23 minutes.

Better from City, with Foden turning after receiving the ball between the lines. Then Anderson flashes a cross across the penalty area from an inside right position, but Haaland was slightly on his heels and it runs out for a goal kick.

Interesting to see Guimaraes drop all the way into Arsenal’s penalty area for their goal-kick a few minutes ago. Arsenal had massive problems playing out from the back against City in the Carabao Cup final last season. The Brazilian’s positioning could be a reaction to that.

Considering Arsenal are missing Saliba, Timber and Rice, their defence has looked relatively untroubled so far. City’s big names in attacking areas are on the pitch, but still finding their level as the new season approaches.

Arsenal have a corner after Gvardiol sticks out a leg to block Madueke’s low cross. Sharp in midfield from Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to spread the play to the right winger. Good delivery from Madueke, headed clear, before White does well to usher the ball behind for another corner.

Gabriel and Khusanov tangle at the back post, appeals for an Arsenal penalty, but Gabriel was the first player to pull a shirt.

Gvardiol with a diagonal cross that floats behind for an Arsenal goal kick. City starting to enjoy some control in the Arsenal half, with Arteta’s team trusting their defensive shape to absorb pressure.

Arsenal with the chance to counter-attack with runners after Kovacic’s loss of possession in midfield, but Odegaard’s pass was slightly behind Madueke, who then had to check before hesitating. Surely more goals to follow, given the ease with which Arsenal are getting at City and the forward quality in Maresca’s team.

Odegaard tries a chipped pass into Havertz’s path in the penalty area but Gvardiol heads away. Moments earlier, Doku claimed he was fouled by White near the touchline but nothing doing.

Arsenal continue to flow forward, finding plenty of space in City’s half, but Tzolis’s cross deflects into the arms of Donnarumma.

There was a check for offside in the build up to Arsenal’s goal but the goal stands. Welcome back VAR, and consider the curtain raised on the new season. City enjoying some possession since conceding.

That’s certainly one way to start a new season. It’s a fabulous team goal, with Lewis-Skelly at the heart of it. There has been a lot of talk about this teenager’s future but, in this reporter’s humble opinion, it should not even be a discussion. Losing a player of this quality, a product of the club’s academy, would be a terrible mistake.

Surely the fastest goal in the history of this fixture, or most fixtures for that matter.

Arsenal were camped in City’s half from kick off, and it was superb from Lewis-Skelly in midfield to let the ball run across his body and find the run of Calafiori with a reverse pass, and the left-back keeps his cool to roll the ball beyond Donnarumma.

Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs

Arsenal get the game, and the 2026-27 domestic season, started.

Former Man City player Mike Summerbee, who fans used to hail with a Small Faces-inspired chant, is involved in the preliminaries.

With no Timber, Saliba or Rice, this could be a more open game than some of the recent chess matches between these sides. The lower stakes should help with that. City have a favourable match up down their left with O’Reilly and Doku against Madueke and White. There is more ball retention in Arsenal’s team than at periods of last season, with Guimaraes, Odegaard, Lewis-Skelly and Havertz in the middle.

Sincere commiserations to the Arsenal and Manchester City supporters who have attempted to travel by road to Cardiff today. We should have nothing but sympathy for those diehards who have tried to navigate the car parks of the M5 and the M4 and nothing but scorn for whoever is in charge of planning at Wembley. Who would have thought to check the football calendar before booking a concert for the week before the new season? A total nonsense. Let’s hope the game turns out to be better than the travel.

Always a talking point during the Six Nations, but there is no reason for it to close on a sunny afternoon on the banks of the River Taff. That will mean a slightly annoying shadow across the pitch, always a potential irritant in these August or May showpieces.

I said already in the last days, no matter if we are in August or May, it is a final and when it is a final we need to win.

[Players coming back from the World Cup] Many, many players, for us for them, we are in the exact same situation. It depends how we can manage the game, we will see.

[What he expects from Anderson] Exactly the player he is. We are not asking him something more. He is a good player on and off the ball, always making an effort for his team-mates.

I said in the press conference, we are going to decide the four captains when the window closes. At the moments, Ruben Dias and Erling are with us [no comment on Rodri’s future].

Good afternoon from Cardiff, where the sun is shining and the fans are enjoying the pubs outside the Principality Stadium. The teams are allowed nine substitutes today, which has really highlighted the bloated nature of Arsenal’s squad. There’s no space for Ethan Nwaneri, Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus, Fabio Vieira or Reiss Nelson. All five of them could be sold by the end of the month.

I had plenty of rest, some work as well, it was a break that I really enjoyed.

Very much [on if he was impressed with his signings]. Christos [Tzolis] came early which always helps with a new signing, and Bruno joined us last week after a long summer with him but he is in good condition.

I think it is something very individual. [Declan] Rice played more than 65 games, he needed a complete rest and we need to build him. It’s not only physical, it’s mental freshness. For the players not involved in the World Cup it is a bit different. They remain so competitive. They wanted to be involved and that’s good to see as well.

[On Bruno] He is a ball of energy. He has an unbelievable desire to win every ball. You sense he will drive the dressing room and when you bring someone with that competitive nature, it will only drive the boys.

[On retaining the title] Still recognise the big margins that we have to improve as a team, individually and as well the ambition of the club which is unquestionable.

Elliot Anderson makes his first City appearance, and he will be partnered by Mateo Kovacic in midfield with Nico O’Reilly drifting into those areas from midfield. Phil Foden, who did not go to the World Cup, starts ahead of Rayan Cherki and Doku, Haaland and Semenyo is City’s strongest front three. No Rodri, but Jack Grealish is on the bench.

Man City starting XI: Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly; Kovacic, Anderson; Semenyo, Foden, Doku; Haaland

Subs: Rulli, Guéhi, Marmoush, Cherki, Nico, Grealish, Aït-Nouri, Nunes, Lewis

The other interesting snippets are Arteta plumping for Madueke over Max Dowman on the right, Havertz over Gyokeres and Calafiori over Hincapie. Also worth noting that there is no place in the squad for Ethan Nwaneri nor Gabriel Martinelli who have been linked with moves. The same goes for Fabio Vieira, Gabriel Jesus and Reiss Nelson.

Arsenal starting XI: Raya; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimaraes, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard; Madueke, Havertz, Tzolis

Subs: Kepa, Hincapie, Rice, Zubimendi, Merino, Eze, Dowman, Saka, Gyokeres

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Mikel names a strong starting XI 👊🤝Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/bckDyMazRo

Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka are with the group, but they have not kicked a ball in pre-season. They are looking at half hour of football at the absolute maximum today.

In case any Arsenal fan had forgotten that last season ended with them losing a Champions League final on penalties, City fans are on hand to remind them. They have one European Cup to Arsenal’s zero. Away from the tin foil trophies, I’m sure much bottle-related mirth is on the cards, especially now broadcasters and fans are aware of the viral possibilities. Too aware, I would argue.

The pool of players who can improve the Premier League champions and Champions League finalists is a small one, but it is still fair to point out that Arsenal’s summer has not gone smoothly. They pursued Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior without success, and Arteta’s desire to take the team to a “different dimension” has so far gone unfulfilled., certainly in the forward positions.

Arsenal still look strong, but have they passed up a chance to pull away from the rest? Sam Wallace takes a look at their summer so far.

It would have been less stressful for Guardiola to go once he realised the great side of Kevin De Bruyne was nearing its end. Instead he opted to oversee a rebuild that gives his successor a greater chance of immediate success, going close to the title last season in what was effectively year one for a re-emerging City side. Guardiola must have known he was signing Gianluigi Donnarumma, Antoine Semenyo, Marc Guéhi and Rayan Cherki for someone else’s long-term benefit.

The Community Shield returns to Cardiff’s Principality Stadium for the first time since 2006, and a different dynamic is at play between Arsenal and Manchester City.

When the two clubs played at Wembley in this fixture three years ago, it felt like a more significant occasion for Arsenal as they sought to prove that the gap was closing to Pep Guardiola’s champions.

Now it is Arsenal and Mikel Arteta who have a league title behind them, while Enzo Maresca is the manager hoping to build credibility as City turn the page post-Pep Guardiola.

In truth, these two teams will look very different by the time the season gathers pace in autumn. World Cup exertions mean Elliot Anderson, Erling Haaland, Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka will be minimally involved in this game, while transfer plans remain up in the air for both camps.

City appear bound to lose Rodri, in addition to Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders in central midfield. Rodri’s sale would expedite a move for Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, and possibly Enzo Fernandez despite Chelsea’s insistence that the deadline to sign him for £120m has passed.

Arsenal are also open for business, hoping to add a right-sided defender to help them cope with William Saliba’s absence. The £75m purchase of Bruno Guimarães means the champions’ midfield options look formidable, but so far it has been another summer without a level-raising forward signing. Christos Tzolis in and Leandro Trossard out looks canny business, but falls into the category of like for like.

Although Arsenal held their nerve to see off City in the title race, they failed to win in three attempts against their rivals, including a limp defeat in the Carabao Cup final at Wembley. Arsenal also failed to win, or score, against Liverpool in the Premier League last season so their record in the big games is an area for improvement.

The victors this afternoon will claim to have laid a marker down, the losers will write the game off as a warm up exercise.

#1947. West Ham’s Answer Was There All Along – So Why Ignore It?

West Ham United’s lack of cutting edge against Preston North End was concerning, but perhaps the most frustrating aspect of Saturday’s 1-1 draw was that Scott Parker already appears to have the answer to the Hammers’ creative problems.

At the risk of sounding like a scratched record, West Ham have an emergency, break-glass solution to breaking teams down. It’s called Jarrod Bowen, and I’m not entirely sure I’ve ever seen our captain play wider than he did at the London Stadium yesterday.

What’s particularly puzzling is that I genuinely believe the best we’ve seen Bowen play in the last couple of years came during the second half against Cardiff City. On that occasion, Parker was effectively handed a blueprint for getting the best out of West Ham’s most important player, yet we’ve barely seen it since.

During that extraordinary second-half comeback against Cardiff, Bowen was given a certain amount of freedom, perhaps encouraged by Parker or maybe he just took it upon himself to drift into the middle of the pitch and cause havoc.

Whatever the reason, he had a hand in all three West Ham goals, and the difference was remarkable.

For the first, he drifted into what might be regarded as the number 10 position and chipped a lovely ball over the Cardiff back line for Divine Mukasa to finish.

The second was similar, with Bowen again creating the opening from a central position. His pass found Joël Piroe, whose flick released Arne Engels to score.

The third goal saw Bowen back in his more familiar position on the right-hand side, where he supplied a wonderful inswinging cross for Max Kilman to equalise.

Jarrod Bowen was given license to roam against Cardiff

But that only went to show quite how much freedom Bowen had. In essence, he was everywhere.

As a blueprint, Scott Parker couldn’t have been given a better gift on his first day in charge than discovering that West Ham’s best player could operate with devastating effect from a free role.

Indeed, I was so encouraged by what I saw that I subsequently wrote about how Scott Parker must restore West Ham’s most dangerous weapon following the defeat at Blackburn.

Because for a brief period against Cardiff, it looked as though we’d stumbled upon something rather special.

Therefore, I was a little underwhelmed that we didn’t see it repeated against Blackburn and very worried when we probably saw our captain more straightjacketed than ever against Preston North End.

If I could offer Parker one piece of encouragement or advice, it would be to get the best out of Bowen.

I’m quite sure our new head coach will improve the defence, and I think we saw signs of that yesterday, albeit against the league’s worst team.

But it can’t come at the expense of shackling our best player, who potentially could only be here for a few more months.

As I argued in my assessment of the Preston draw, West Ham had plenty of possession, shots and territory, but very little magic.

And that’s the really bloody annoying part. We have a player who can provide exactly that, but we’re asking him to operate in a way which makes life considerably easier for the opposition.

I know one thing. If I was head coach of an opposition Championship team and I saw Jarrod Bowen shackled to the right wing, I’d breathe a huge sigh of relief.

If we don’t succeed in getting promotion, Bowen could leave for a pittance of £15m. That’s the release clause in the revised contract he agreed following relegation.

We do know that Bowen flew to Prague to meet Daniel Křetínský before pledging to remain at West Ham for another season, as he explained in his interview with Sky Sports.

And I’m now very fearful that we are going to waste what should really be something of a cheat code for the division.

Bowen is comfortably our best attacking player, and we’ve already seen how devastating he can be when allowed to roam. Yet rather than building upon that discovery, Parker appears to have returned him to a position where he’s easier to mark and less able to influence the game.

I wish it weren’t so, but I’ve now come to the conclusion that the second half against Cardiff was a pure accident rather than a window into what we could begin to see from Scott Parker as he got his teeth into the West Ham job.

But decisions like that could well make the difference between automatic promotion and a play-off place, if we’re lucky.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

With over a decade of professional sports media experience, he is a frequent West Ham United analyst and contributor for Sky Sports News, BBC Football Focus, and BBC Radio 5 Live. He previously served as an official video and content creator for West Ham United FC during the club's tenure at Upton Park and featured in the official documentary commemorating the historic final game at the Boleyn Ground.

A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.

The problem with that is you need two players wide to stretch defensive teams, by all means give Bowen a free role, but who do you play right wing, Solomon or KWP?

#1946. 3 Positives and 3 Negatives to take from Newcastle 2 Arsenal 2

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Ahead of each game we ask one of our writers to come up with three positives and three negatives following the match.

Plenty to talk about after this Premier League game.

Newcastle United a goal down at the  break having been totally outplayed by the league leaders, only for then a very different second half.

The only place to start is the way that the team responded after the break.

It was a real tonic after recent home games. The changes worked and they came to life, leaving the Premier League champions rattled

If we really are in a process of rebuilding then the manager was right when he said that this second half spell is what they have to aim for more often.

Lewis Miley had a really good game in his proper position in the centre of midfield, and it was Bruno came off second best, at times.

It was frustrating to see Sean Steur hooked at half time but Jacob Ramsey showed up well when he came off the bench along with Elanga.

Miley is still such a young player, which highlights that we have a great talent on our hands.

It helps ease the pain of letting Elliot Anderson slip through our grasp.

Many hours before this game kicked off, I was of the mind that I’d snap hands off for a draw against Arsenal.

We were at least able to match them in spells.

A point against them might just well be one of those that proves extremely valuable come the end of the season.

The first half contained all of the drift we have seen too many times this season.

If your glass is half empty, then the fightback could be a case of a stopped clock being right twice a day.

Some concerns definitely do remain about our direction and the input of the new manager in this post-Eddie Howe era, the so-called Newcastle 2.0.

Another winning position has been thrown away.

The same thing happened down at Fulham. It drives you crackers at times.

They surely must have to work on how to see a game out? It’s not rocket science.

The manager gets paid to pick the team, and that will always be a talking point.

However, Jaissle left a lot of players out of this game, a total of around £260m worth no less.

Toure and Bamba were also omitted from the actual match day squad.

Wasn’t Toure doing really well when he played over in Germany? Why is he deemed nowhere near for a Premier League game when he’s got bags of pace and skill to burn?

Were these two players signed as first teamers for this season?

I’ve seen reports saying that the manager is calling for more recruitment in January. It’s all a bit baffling.

#1945. “Superb” – Parker’s delight over reversing Nuno’s biggest mistake | West Ham News

24 hours on from West Ham’s  tepid point against the bottom side in the league and whilst the justified criticism is flying around, there are definitely positives to pull out of a fixture in which West Ham dominated all the important statistics save the most important one: The points tally at the final whistle.

Sadly, again the Hammers have lost ground on the leaders and now sit eight points adrift. And yet, from Scott Parker’s comments, there are definite signs that he’s learned from at least some of the mistakes made by his predecessor. Reversing Nuno’s decision to cast out Edson Alvarez from the senior team proved a massive success.. Who knew.

Yesterday’s re-integration of ‘El Machin’ into the starting line up was his first league appearance in a West Ham shirt since May 2025.

This was an Alvarez playing more like his first season as a Hammer.

As Scott Parker summed up, Alvarez did not let him down:

“He brought every bit of what we needed. It’s a young team, and his experience today in terms of organising and his general presence on the pitch was very, very good for us for large aspects.

“It was a big ask and I knew that going into the game, he hasn’t played at all this year and probably hasn’t had a lot of training in and around the first team. But I just felt his experience and know-how around it was needed, and for sure he was a massive part today of why we performed the way we performed” (Justin Allen- YouTube)

The Mexican clearly cares: He was in tears before kick off, so tough has his time in the football wilderness been.

Having been such a critic of him during his card-strewn Lopetegui era, credit where it is due. Edson Alvarez was, indeed, excellent yesterday and it is a testimony to his professionalism that he played a full ninety after not playing competitive football since August.

If he can maintain that kind of focus and form, Parker may well have found the missing piece in West Ham’s defensive jigsaw puzzle, that proved beyond his predecessor who simply wouldn’t extend the olive branch to any of his ‘frozen out’ players.

#1944. Newcastle United Game Management issue is huge Red Herring

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

The issue of Newcastle United Game Management has reared its head once again.

It always hurts when you take the lead and end up drawing, or even worse, lose.

Especially if it is a late goal that is conceded.

After the 2-2 draw with Arsenal, I have heard and read a fair few fans questioning the Newcastle United Game Management.

What these fans are questioning, is basically whyafter coming back to lead against Arsenal with 62 minutes on the clock, why couldn’t Matthias Jaissle and his players see out the rest of the match without conceding?

The 3 positives and 3 negatives piece on The Mag this Monday morning perfectly summed up the kind of thing I have been seeing.

David Punton selecting ‘Game Management’ as one of his three negatives and saying: ‘Another winning position has been thrown away. The same thing happened down at Fulham. It drives you crackers at times. They surely must have to work on how to see a game out? It’s not rocket science.’

So is this true, the Newcastle United Game Management a huge issue?

First of all I have had a look at the 14 Newcastle United matches this season from purely a statistical viewpoint.

Do Newcastle United repeatedly take the lead and throw it away?

Newcastle United when scoring the opening goal of the game this season, what ended up the final result? Won 4 (Spurs, Millwall, Hull, Palace), Drawn 2 (Liverpool, Fulham) Lost 0

Newcastle United when conceding the opening goal of the game this season, what ended up the final result? Won 1 (West Brom), Drawn 2 (Bournemouth, Arsenal) Lost 5 (Leeds, Coventry, Villa, Everton x2)

Which matches have Newcastle United scored the final goal of the game? Happened seven times (West Brom, Spurs, Bournemouth, Millwall, Leeds, Palace, Everton cup)

Which matches have Newcastle United conceded the final goal of the game? Happened seven times (Liverpool, Hull, Coventry, Villa, Everton, Fulham, Arsenal)

In his Positives and Negatives piece, David Punton says about the supposed failings of Newcastle United Game Management: ‘They surely must have to work on how to see a game out? It’s not rocket science.’

I am not just having a go at David here but what exactly is this magical way of ensuring that there is zero chance of allowing the opposition to score once you have taken the lead?

Newcastle United went 2-1 up on 62 minutes, so Arsenal had what turned out to be 37 minutes to get an equaliser (and then potential winner…).

They are the best team in the Premier League and have the strongest bench.

What is the absolute certain route to not letting them score?

As the stats show above, Newcastle United have given as good as they have got this season when it comes to scoring first and the eventual result, compared to the games when the opposition have scored first.

If you are leading by a single goal and it is the last minute of a match, then all your defenders recklessly charge up the pitch and you concede, that would be really poor Newcastle United Game Management.

It would be really poor Newcastle United Game Management if leading and then gifted an equaliser when trying a daft risky pass on the edge of your own penalty area.

This didn’t happen on Saturday, nor indeed at Fulham in the previous match.

Arsenal scored with 21 minutes left to play when some excellent play got them up the pitch and Madueke scored a good goal, which even though it went through a Newcastle defender’s legs you think Lukas Hornicek should have saved it.

Newcastle scored in the 80th minute at Craven Cottage and Fulham had to throw everything at them, they got the benefit of a bit of a scramble in our penalty area and two deflections contributed to their equaliser.

This isn’t disastrous Newcastle United Game Management, this is football.

It is a huge Red Herring to claim this is a serious problem this season for Matthias Jaissle and his team.

Mikel Arteta’s side totally dominating the opening 45 minutes.

BBC Sport journalist Alex Howell giving these comments on the Newcastle United players and a rating for each.

#1942. West Ham’s home problem summed up in one sentence – by a Preston fan

Preston North End, the bottom side in the Championship, arrived in east London yesterday unaffected by the occasion and kept West Ham at bay for an hour until Dinos Mavropanos headed equaliser restored parity and saved Scott Parker’s blushes.

Two weeks’ work during the international break had accounted for very little as Preston withstood everything the Hammers and their almost 60,000 fans had to throw at their lowly opponents.

And therein lies the problem. Having surrendered the small, intimidating, sometimes downright hostile atmosphere of Upton Park back in 2016, the distance from the pitch and the wide open spaces of the Olympic Stadium are about as intimidating as a day out at London Zoo for our opponents and their fans who continue to pour scorn on the venue.

It just doesn’t strike fear into opponents as it should. Even when we score.

Isolated tiers in the stadium and poor pitch proximity do little to help the atmosphere at the London Stadium – as our opponents are finding out

Preston fan Tm Mercer, writing in the Lancashire Evening Post, makes it abundantly clear that there was no noticeable crowd reaction to lift the home side, as there should have been once Mavropanos restored parity:

“Aside from play-off finals, I’m pretty certain it is the first time I’ve been in a stadium for a league match with 60,000-plus through the gate.

Yet, when they equalised, it did not feel like the roar of that many people in such a cavernous ground. Give me somewhere like Gigg Lane, stood in their paddock pitch side, any day!”

For the uninitiated, Gigg Lane is the home of Bury FC with a capacity of around…..12,000.

Nobody is suggesting the Hammers fans were silent. The cursèd accoustics from the soulless bowl and sheer distance from the pitch play right into opponents’ hands.  And, ten years after moving in, it’s going to take a lot more than some safe standing and a couple of family zones to fix it.

#1941. Eddie Howe and Jason Tindall deliver ‘exclusive football masterclass’ at school and inspiring Q&A

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Nothing had been heard of Eddie Howe and Jason Tindall since their official departure from Newcastle United at the end of July.

Apart that is from endless speculation about where the duo might end up next.

Manchester United of course recently speculated as a likely destination for Eddie Howe (and presumably Jason Tindall and most of the rest of Howe’s NUFC backroom team).

Mauricio Pochettino has of course taken on that particular poisoned chalice at Man U (and got off to a great start at Anfield!).

The radio silence on Eddie Howe ended at the weekend and we covered it on The Mag. The former NUFC boss having moved back down to the south coast and Southampton manager Tonda Eckert revealed that Eddie Howe had visited the Saints’ training ground and they’d had a chat.

This has now quickly been followed by a school making public that both Eddie Howe and Jason Tindall have paid them a visit.

The pair visiting Bromley High School GDST, with the school giving a rundown of what happened on the day.

The school stating: ‘Bromley High School students were treated to an unforgettable day of top flight sport as former Newcastle United Manager Eddie Howe and Assistant Manager Jason Tindall visited the school to deliver an exclusive football masterclass and an inspiring Q&A session.’

A few snippets from their report of the day:

‘When asked what defines a great leader, Howe emphasised that leadership begins with personal standards rather than titles. He encouraged students to focus on everyday habits, such as being the first to arrive, the last to leave and treating peers with kindness and integrity. Howe told the students, noting that trustworthiness and consistency are what truly earn the respect of teammates and classmates. Tindall echoed this sentiment, adding that genuine leadership means supporting others and leading through actions rather than words.’

Navigating Pressure and Building Resilience

‘Students asked how top-flight managers handle team selection, media scrutiny, and setbacks. Howe explained that he and Tindall rely on honest, consistent processes, focusing on training effort and tactical preparation rather than outside noise. He also praised Tindall’s loyalty and behind-the-scenes support, highlighting how strong partnerships rely on trust and unity even when difficult decisions are made.

Discussing how athletes bounce back from mistakes, both coaches stressed the importance of blocking out social media negativity and leaning on trusted support networks, coaches, teammates, family and friends. Howe shared how breaking challenges down into simple, achievable steps helps players regain confidence, while Tindall noted how achieving major milestones can fuel lasting self-belief.’

‘In response to a question about player development, Howe shared examples of how dedication and adaptability pay off at the highest level, from players staying after training every day to perfect their technical skills to others successfully transitioning into entirely new positions on the pitch. Howe told the students natural talent must always be matched by a relentless work ethic and coachability.

The duo also highlighted the vital role of the wider squad, noting that a positive attitude and commitment behind the scenes are what truly drive team culture, drawing a direct parallel to school sports teams.’

#1940. One selection choice boosts January transfer fund by millions | West Ham News

Switching several key players after the international break was a brave move designed to revitalise West Ham’s fortunes. Had the ball not crashed against the woodwork four times but nestled in the corner just once we’d all be proclaiming his changes as astute: Bringing back Alvarez and switching Morato to a centre back role weren’t rocket science but shored up a hitherto leaky defence.

However, bringing Fin Herrick into the side – ostensibly ‘resting’ (a.k.a.’dropping’) Hermansen – paid off . With Herrick now tried and tested, his elevation to credible first team keeper surely puts paid to any interest West Ham were showing in young Swansea ‘keeper Joe Duncan.

Herrick’s emergence means the budget doesn’t have to be diluted: Koppen can call off the search for a ‘keeper and find a goal scorer instead.

As Matt’s Claret and Hugh article last week predicted: “West Ham Could Save Themselves A Transfer Fee” by promoting Herrick rather than forking out millions to bring another promising young goal keeper to West Ham – when there’s one in situ already.

Exactly as it has seemed to pan out. Whilst Parker claims Hermansen has been strategically withdrawn for ‘some air’, there’s every chance that Herrick will get more match time whilst Areola remains unfit. And good luck to him. As he proved yesterday he’s got what it takes to keep a modest attack at bay.

A sterner test will come at Portsmouth but saving Koppen’s transfer budget for the acquisition of a striker who can actually hit the target looks to be the 100% absolute stone-cold priority in January, if it isn’t already too late.

And Herrick’s emergence has probably boosted the funds available to Koppen significantly.

#1938. Absolutely appalling abuse for Dan Burn from Newcastle United fans after he said this

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

If you hadn’t heard of Dan Burn and somebody detailed his journey in football, there is no way you would believe it.

Santiago Munez and Goal! sounds like a very believable factual documentary in comparison.

Dan Burn one of countless kids taken on by the Newcastle United Academy but don’t make it.

In his case, it was at the age of 11 when told his dream ended there.

The rest is history. Though you would be forgiven if you double checked certain facts because they sound like the work of somebody’s very active imagination.

Dan Burn who entered the world of men’s football with Darlington at non-league level, whilst working part-time collecting shopping trolleys at ASDA.

Through grit, determination and of course ability, Dan Burn developed a very decent career for himself, playing for Fulham, Yeovil, Wigan, Birmingham and Brighton.

This career not standing out as a stellar one, but certainly a very decent life in football, with a fair few Premier League appearances amongst his 300+ games across the years.

Then just over three months ahead of his 30th birthday, Dan Burn got the call that was going to change his life forever.

Inheriting a desperate mid-season relegation fight when taking the Newcastle United job in November 2021, two months later Eddie Howe was looking to bring in ready to play Premier League experienced players to avoid instant disaster for the then new Newcastle United owners.

Kieran Trippier, Chris Wood and Matt Targett arrived at St James’ Park in January 2022, with Brighton reluctantly allowing Dan Burn to join that trio for a reported £13m transfer fee. Eddie Howe and the Newcastle United owners were ridiculed by many journalists, pundits and fans of other clubs. Tagged as the ‘richest’ club owners in world football and yet they and their manager thought Dan Burn was the kind of signing they needed. Hilarious. Bruno Guimaraes also arrived in that same transfer window but he was aimed at the longer-term, new to the Premier League it would be March 2022 before he started a game for NUFC, by which point United were well on their way to safety with Burn, Targett and Wood playing key roles in that, Kieran Trippier also started well but very quickly picked up a significant injury and only returned at the very end of that season.

With relegation avoided, Eddie Howe brought in the exciting young Dutch left-footed central defender Sven Botman, who when he was 20 turning 21 played a key role in a stunning Ligue 1 title success for Lille.

With the summer 2022 signing of Botman, I don’t think any Newcastle fan would have been surprised if Dan Burn had then ended up becoming a squad player. Instead he became a player that Eddie Howe picked every match with very few exceptions. Matt Targett picked up an injury very early that 2022-23 season and Dan Burn was moved to left-back.

The back five that played almost every Premier League match that 2022-23 season was Pope, Trippier, Schar, Botman Burn.

The ‘experts’ couldn’t believe it, Eddie Howe and Newcastle United finished fourth in the Premier League and qualified for the Champions League, plus NUFC got to their first Wembley final in 24 years.

That success was massively built on an astonishing defensive record.

Manchester City won the 2022-23 Premier League title only conceding 33 goals in the 38 league matches, this Newcastle United five matched that low goals conceded total. In the six Carabao Cup matches that got United to Wembley, only two goals were conceded across the half dozen matches.

Eddie Howe had created something very special at Newcastle United and Dan Burn was one of the first names on the team sheet, whether playing in the centre of defence or left-back.

Dan Burn finally living the Newcastle United dream in his 30s.

He was somebody the fans could really relate to, many of us kidding ourselves that if only things had worked out a little differently, that could have been you or me instead of Dan Burn in a Newcastle United shirt. That wasn’t the reality of course but that is how Dan Burn makes you feel. That he is a Newcastle United fan who by that sheer grit and determination is playing for NUFC, rather than watching them.

We have had many other homegrown heroes, many in my lifetime, but Alan Shearer had this incredible talent for scoring goals that elevated him above all others in the Premier League, whilst Peter Beardsley and Paul Gascoigne just had incredible talent that for me matches any player I have ever seen play football for any club or country.

As for Dan Burn, he has continued to be phenomenal in the colours of Newcastle United.

The 2023-24 was one of the worst ever for Newcastle United injuries, all but mission impossible for Eddie Howe and his small squad to lose so many players so often, plus the disastrous Sandro Tonali suspension. With the squad hit by so many injuries, when Dan Burn picked up a serious one to his back, he came back far earlier than the medical staff wanted him to because the manager, team and fans needed him. Newcastle United still managed 60 EPL points that 2023-24 season and came so close to qualifying from their Champions League group which was as tough as it could possibly be. One opponent reached the final and another the semi-final. United were cheated in Paris out of a famous win that would have led to them qualifying instead of PSG. In the stunning 4-1 home win over PSG, Dan Burn was immense at the back and scored THAT goal.

The finances meant Newcastle United didn’t buy any new first team players in summer 2024 and indeed a PSR crisis that had to be dealt with in June 2024 meant Elliot Anderson and Yankuba Minteh were sold. Dan Burn and his Newcastle United team-mates reacted by producing the most successful season in living memory for most of us. Another Champions League qualification. Oh..and a trophy. The unforgettable sight of Dan Burn scoring the best headed goal Wembley (new or old) has ever seen. Burn one of United’s very best players that magical day, a trophy finally lifted on 16 March 2025.

The 2025-26 season proved far too much for a still too small Newcastle United squad to cope with a 58 game season, especially as injuries piled up once again. Including Dan Burn the victim of a cowardly challenge during the away derby mix, the Geordie warrior wanted to try and play on, even though it was later discovered he’d punctured a lung and broken a rib. As always, his commitment was immense during such a challenging season.

The perfect choice to be the new Newcastle United captain, injury delayed his 2026-27 season kicking off. No surprise that things significantly improved at the back when Dan Burn was able to start in the Premier League. After conceding 14 goals in the opening seven Premier League matches, the next three saw only two conceded (against Palace, Everton and Fulham). Then Dan Burn leading Newcastle United to Saturday’s comeback draw against an Arsenal side that had won nine of their opening ten EPL matches.

Dan Burn getting absolutely appalling abuse from Newcastle United fans

In recent days a video has circulated online, Dan Burn stopped and asked for one of those one minute video interviews, where random questions are fired and only need a name as the answer.

I’m not sure when the video interview happened but my guess is that Dan Burn was stopped as he went into the Newcastle United Foundation dinner last week, which was to raise funds for the charity and to celebrate local achievers.

These are the questions and answers, I have changed the order in which they were asked, see if you can guess which one has prompted the abuse aimed at Dan Burn.

Best player played against – Ronaldo Funniest player – Jacob Murphy Best leader – Jordan Henderson Best finisher – Harry Kane Best on a night out – Lewis Dunk Best player you have played with – Alexander Isak Biggest prankster – David Perkins Toughest played against – Adama Traore Most famous person on your phone – Sam Fender

It is important to point out that those Newcastle United fans giving Dan Burn this appalling abuse are only some Newcastle United fans, not all NUFC fans.

Of course I don’t know if every single one of them who are giving abuse is a Newcastle fan but certainly many of them are. As it is online you can see that they regularly post comments about NUFC and I have no doubt these people are Newcastle fans.

So just in case you were still wondering which answer has prompted all of this abuse, it is Dan Burn saying Alexander Isak is the best player he has played with.

Apparently this is an unforgivable crime, at least for some Newcastle United fans.

That this then justifies saying what a useless football player Dan Burn is AND far far worse, these fans aiming abuse at him as a person, his character.

Everybody is of course entitled to their own opinion BUT I can’t even attempt to get my head around why anyone would have this opinion AND even worse, be desperate to tell everyone else.

The best thing about social media is that everybody can now have their say.

The worst thing about social media is that everybody can now have their say.

I have no doubt that if Dan Burn sees these abusive comments he will just brush them to one side. It is just a fact that people get abuse online, especially if they are famous.

It depresses me the way many Newcastle United fans go on at times. One match, even one moment in a match, can see some Newcastle United fans giving one of our players ridiculous levels of criticism, even if they have done incredible things for the club and fans. It is like those fans who now want us to believe that Eddie Howe simply got lucky with the success he brought to NUFC, that he just stumbled along and it as all down to others why Newcastle United were suddenly winning football matches, getting to Wembley, playing in the Champions League and….winning a trophy.

This abuse for Dan Burn though, it really does my head in.

Why would any Newcastle United fan think it is appropriate?

To me, Dan Burn represents everything that is positive about Newcastle United and the people of our region.

If you asked him to run through a brick wall for Newcastle United, he would ask which one he should run through first.

Dan Burn makes me proud to be a Newcastle United fan, proud to be a Geordie.

He has been brilliant for Newcastle United, brought us so much joy, whilst off the pitch he is the same.

Countless charity events and also brave enough to talk about his mental health struggles of the past, in order to help others.

Dan Burn names the BEST player he’s ever played with 🤝🔥 https://t.co/4eqSbEhB6a

— All Out Football (@ItsAllOutFooty) November 17, 2026

Nobody is above criticism but I would love to see some Newcastle United fans just tone it down a bit. Instead of unleashing hate aimed at some of the best amongst us, have a think before giving a reaction.

I have heard fans talk about a tough run of Newcastle United fixtures.

I had a quick look at the upcoming Newcastle United fixtures and I think it gives a really positive outlook.

Obviously no Premier League game looks easy this season BUT some are easier than others.

Put it this way, would you prefer to play teams that are generally winning matches and are towards the top of the Premier League, or those who generally aren’t winning and are towards the bottom?

After that excellent 2-2 draw with league leaders Arsenal, Newcastle next play second top Brighton away. The Seagulls having lost 2-0 at Hull yesterday.

Following that though, Newcastle play three of the bottom five. Man U and Sunderland are both in the relegation zone and have to visit St James’ Park, then United travel to Ipswich who are fifth bottom.

As things currently stand, Newcastle United have played five of the top seven in the Premier League and only one of the bottom five in the table.

Writing this before the Brentford v Everton match on Monday night, there are eight more Newcastle United fixtures before NUFC have played all 19 teams.

These eight left to play are currently placed in the Premier League table 2nd, 3rd, 8th, 10th, 16th, 17th, 18th, 19th.

Looking at these Newcastle United fixtures that are coming up and then looking at the Premier League table, I think it is fair to say that NUFC have had a tough start to the season and no reason why they can’t start to pick up more points.

Of course we will need to see more of the kind of form Newcastle United showed in the second half on Saturday against Arsenal, a little less of what they showed in the first half.

#1935. West Ham’s striker woes put into sharp relief after yet another goal

Scott Parker’s decision to recall Soungoutou Magassa from the ‘Nuno wilderness’ back into the West Ham fold looks well founded.

Similarly, the apparent re-integration of Edson Alvarez into West Ham United’s starting eleven last weekend has been met with almost universal approval after the Mexican’s decent showing against Preston.

At the very least, these two players will see their transfer values rise simply by being deployed in competitive football. At best, they could contribute significantly towards a successful outcome for the club this season.

All of which makes Niclas Fullkrug’s escapades in Germany even more ironic, as West Ham’s failure to score their winner after thirty attempts gets put into sharp relief by their on-loan striker becoming the Bundesliga’s top scorer.

Another goal by Fullkrug at the weekend in Bremen’s 4- 0 victory will make Hammers fans scratch their head and wonder whether, with different coaching and different attitudes, the German could have made an impact in east London this season. He’d certainly have got some game time.

Fullkrug is now the top scorer in the German league after his ninth goal for Werder Bremen at the weekend

Too late to think about recalling Fullkrug, it seems he’s found his spiritual ‘home’, and good luck to him.

It does throw the coaching failures of the last three of West Ham’s so called ‘managers’ sharply into focus when they all relied heavily on their favourites and ‘fell out’ frequently with players: Who can forget Lopetegui’s dressing room bust-ups with Mohammed Kudus and Jean-Clair Todibo?

Eye-watering sums are spent by football clubs on researching, scouting and recruiting players, but then whole careers seem ended on a managerial whim or a clash of egos.

By no means unique to West Ham, but it is an area in which clubs have to learn to do better or risk losing, as in Fullkrug’s case, the very stars who can fire the goals they’ve just paid through the nose to acquire.

#1934. Report highlights Nuno’s treatment of ‘frozen out’ West Ham players

Mexican Edson Alvarez has received plaudits after his satisfactory return to the West Ham United starting line up following Scott Parker’s decision to re-integrate him into the side. Alvarez’ evident emotional release at being recalled to the team is testimony to the struggle he’s endured both on, and off the pitch since last playing a league game as a West Ham player.

Injury, surgery, kidnapping scandal, covid certificate allegations – all must have taken their toll on the Alvarez family as did Nuno’s decision to freeze the midfielder out of the West Ham team after, it must be said, a pretty decent World Cup.

Here is a player who had not started a competitive fixture since August yet he was ready to go when called upon and lasted a whole 90 minutes. As reported by futnsoccer.com, Nuno’s treatment of the Mexican national team captain evidently took a big toll, and it was only through his own resilience that he was able to jump when Scott Parker called:

“It has been a very difficult period for me after four months without playing, you know? And a lot of things happening in my life, a lot of changes,” Alvarez said.

“Imagine being away from the team, like training alone…..I’ve been working really hard by myself, and I’m just looking forward”.

Emotional and successful return for Edson Alvarez: Who’d have thought it.

Alvarez was so moved that he sought Parker out before the start of the game:

“I spoke with [Parker] at the beginning of the game and I said thank you. I said thank you to him because he is giving me again the opportunity, the chance to show myself, and that means a lot to me.”

“I need to pay him back that confidence, and I think the only way that I can do it is on the pitch; like showing myself, fighting, and doing everything with my experience for the team. I really missed it.”

In a team famously devoid of leadership, it sounds as if Scott Parker has just found himself a lieutenant who will go into battle for him – and for West Ham – any time he’s asked. All of which can only throw into question Nuno’s decision to ‘exile’ Alvarez and so many other players from the training ground.

Alvarez is exactly the type of player we will need to drag us back up the table. I’d like him to engage less with the referee, because that usually only ends up one way, but other than that he’s an excellent asset.

Great point about engaging with the referee, Alan.

It will have been a long, long time since Edson Alvarez was involved in games at Championship level. Just like everyone else, he will need to learn very quickly that there are no reviews and we need to get on with it without the confrontation, protest or the waiting for support and sympathy.

Alvarez did the team talk immediately before kick off. While the attitude of the likes of Todibo were always questionable that did not seem to be the case with Alvarez. Alvarez is fiery but that should be manageable surely, it’s part of why managers are called managers they’re supposed to be able to manage.

#1933. Newcastle United to host 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup matches

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

It has now been revealed that Newcastle United are set to host 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup matches.

The United Kingdom was officially confirmed as the tournament’s host nation on Monday.

The Newcastle United Women’s team official social media declaring that the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup is: ‘Set to be the largest single-sport event ever staged in the UK, the bid features Newcastle among the host cities.’

Newcastle United Women’s star Jordan Nobbs: “Having grown up in the North East, I know how much football means to people here and just how passionate the fans are about the women’s game. The FIFA Women’s World Cup coming to the UK in 2035 is another milestone for our sport, and bringing matches to this region would take the tournament to another level. We’ve seen what happens when the Lionesses play in front of crowds up here – the atmosphere is electric.”

Jordan Nobbs adding: “Hosting these matches wouldn’t just be an incredible celebration of football; it would inspire the next generation of young girls across the North East by showing them that the biggest stage in the world is within their reach.”

BBC Sport state: ‘The English stadiums included in the 2035 bid are: Villa Park, The Amex, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Emirates Stadium, Selhurst Park, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Wembley, Etihad Stadium, St James’ Park, the City Ground, the Stadium of Light and Old Trafford.’

They then add: ‘Cardiff City Stadium and Principality Stadium are the two Welsh venues, with Easter Road in Edinburgh and Hampden Park in Glasgow in Scotland. Northern Ireland missed out on co-hosting the men’s Euros in 2028 after the UK government said in 2024 it would not provide funding to redevelop Casement Park in time – but a redeveloped Windsor Park is set to stage matches in 2035. A further three stadiums could be added – Birmingham’s new Powerhouse Stadium, Wrexham’s redeveloped Racecourse Ground, and a potential new Chelsea ground – which would take the tournament to 16 cities and 22 venues.’

I don’t think any Newcastle United fans should be taking too much from this announcement with regards to whether or not a new stadium will be built, rather than redeveloping St James’ Park.

A new stadium could be built in time to host matches at the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup.

Whilst the club could also withdraw from hosting any games in these next few years and their fixtures given to one or more other stadiums.
