And that is it. Two home defeats by Leeds in less than 80 hours for Forest. Glasner will have much to ponder with a daunting trip to Anfield coming up on Saturday. All smiles for Farke’s side.

A look at a third for Leeds. Aaronson drives forward before setting Wilson who in turn lays on a first-time pass to Calvert-Lewin. The forward attempts to take his shot first time but can’t get the requisite power on the ball to beat Sels.

A pitch invader makes a brief appearance on the turf but is swiftly ushered away.

There is a late chance for Forest. Hutchinson’s cross is helped on by Dominguez but that touch inadvertently takes the ball away from Ndoye at the back post.

Forest fans are filing out of the exits and who can blame them?

That just about sums up Forest’s night. Dominguez stands over a free-kick from a dangerous area and, with the box loaded with their most imposing aerial threats, the midfielder sends the ball well over their heads and out for a goal-kick. So poor.

Calvert-Lewin is now on for Nmecha. Not really the striker Forest defenders would want to see at this stage of the game.

Another set-piece, this time a Stach corner, is barely dealt with by Forest.

There’s a shout for a handball at the other end as Ndoye spears a cross into the body of Elvedi, but the referee rightly waves the appeals away.

The “oles” ring out from the away end as Leeds string a series of passes together in the corner right in front of it. Forest are looking rather helpless here.

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2 (Justin) Ampadu launches a throw-in from the right but has to reload as the referee notices some pushing in the box. His next attempt is far too loopy but causes Forest all sorts of trouble, bouncing and bobbling, and coming all the way through a thicket of limbs to Nmecha at the far post. Williams attempts to keep the ball out from a prone position on the goalline under pressure from Justin, who gets the final touch as the ball is bundled over the line.

It's messy but Leeds won't care! 😁Forest fail to deal with the throw-in and Nmecha is there to bundle it in...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/oV46fs5RmP

Jair goes into the book after catching Ampadu in full flight. He never had a prayer of reaching that ball.

The resulting free-kick lands to Amapadu himself in the box, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

Stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

There’s plenty more endeavour down Forest’s new-look left side. Hudson Odoi scampers down that flank before cutting inside, and while he’s unable to fashion a chance the intent is correct.

The substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

Glasner resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes. Diomande, Aina, Jesus and Kalimuendo are replaced by Murillo, Netz, Ndoye and Hudson Odoi.

Okafor shows off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

Chances at both ends! Kalimuendo plays a wonderful ball into the box for Wood to sweep home but Trafford springs into action and makes a stunning save.

Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

End-to-end football! ⚡️First Wood, then Okafor - just 19 seconds between the two chances 😮#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/TGQmtwLNwE

Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”

This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

Dan James puts Leeds United in front! ⚽️Tidy finish from the Welshman... #EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/GzWg6zLGLm

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 1 (James) We finally have a breakthrough. Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels. The winger has been Leeds’ biggest threat and deserves that goal.

James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

Both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

Should the scores remain level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. There’s still a half to play of course, but Forest’s League Cup shoot-out record should be a source of confidence having won seven from eight.

What a tackle from Joe Rodon! 💥#EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/p5GkzSFEoZ

James wins the ball on the halfway line and feeds Okafor down the left. He attempts a deft through-ball into a thicket of bodies but it comes to nothing.

Leeds circulate the ball, working the ball from side to side but there is nowhere near enough movement in front of the ball-player for any meaningful forward passes to be played.

And, quite aptly, the referee blows up at three seconds past 45 minutes. Certainly not a half for the books.

Another half-chance for Forest! Milenkovic lands on a second ball off a deep free-kick but he cannot keep his strike down. A classic centre-half’s effort if you will.

Ampadu comes over to the left to fire in a long throw-in. Sels comes steaming out of his goal and fumbles the ball but is awarded a free-kick after Muharemovic makes contact. Looked very minimal in all fairness.

Oof, a good chance for Aina! Williams’ cross from the left comes all the way through to his opposite wing-back, but Aina’s half-volley sails over. A cracking contact, though.

Elvedi and Muharemovic look to be astute buys from Leeds’ perspective. Both assured at the back and the latter especially is confident progressing the ball.

Just as I type that Forest threaten with a ball over the top, but Justin nips in to take the ball away from Wood.

Another decent opening for Leeds after a Forest turnover. Nmecha strides through the middle but Milenkovic is in position to ensure his run comes to nothing.

What a tackle! Kalimuendo bursts through the middle after Leeds cede possession in a dangerous position. The winger plays in Wood who looks to be through on goal but Rodon comes out of nowhere to telescope a limb and stop the forward in his tracks. Fantastic defensive work from the Welshman.

Nmecha attempts to break beyond the halfway line but is stymied by a swarm of Forest players. He demands a foul from the referee who is not interested in the least.

It’s then Okafor’s turn to put in a dangerous cross from the left, but Nmecha cannot get to it.

Tanaka becomes the first man to go into the book. The ball gets away from him and Jesus puts body between man and ball smartly to win the foul.

Tanaka is now dropping into the back line to allow Leeds’ defenders the licence to get wider and higher. Forest will need to be wary of their opponents’ numerical advantage down the flanks.

The game has reached something of a holding pattern as both sides resolve to slow things down, at least temporarily. Forest have settled into a slightly deeper block.

Sensing an opportunity, Ampadu spins in a glorious through-ball between centre-back and full-back for James to gallop on to. He hits the by-line and cuts back to Longstaff, but the midfielder can’t beat Sels. A good chance that probably should have been converted.

A good chance goes begging! 🫣Longstaff is free for Leeds but fires it straight at Sels...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/0UJdfSDQ6w

Tanaka then turns provider, winning possession in Forest’s half before playing in Longstaff, whose cross-cum-shot does not threaten Sels’ goal.

Both sides have physical, quick out-balls, which has made for a frenetic encounter thus far. James rasps in another fierce cross from the right after another sweeping Leeds move, but Nmecha cannot get there and Tanaka fires well over on the follow-up.

Aina’s throw-in, this time from the left, is flicked on to Jesus at the back post and while the forward is able to direct the ball goalwards there is Justin on the line to clear the ball to safety.

Chance! Dominguez slides in Aina down the right channel and the full-back’s mishit cross has Trafford scrambling. He palms the ball behind for a corner, which is headed away for a Forest throw-in on the far side.

Leeds are enjoying a spell of possession here, Tanaka and Longstaff peeling off into the wide areas to collect the ball and disrupt Forest’s mid-block out-of-possession structure. The hosts are more than happy for Leeds to circulate the ball in front of their first line of pressure as, for the second time tonight, Trafford boots it out into touch.

Dominguez stands up a smart cross to the far post where Aina is waiting to head back across goal. Trafford backpedals into Kalimuendo and the referee awards Leeds a free-kick.

Wonderful touch there early in the game from none other than Oliver Glasner.

Forest’s head coach perfectly trapped a high ball as it landed towards him in the technical area.

James shows off his speed for the first time tonight, accelerating down the right before fizzing a dangerous ball into the six-yard box but Forest clear their lines.

Sels goes long to Wood (feels like the right play given his attributes), James lands on the second ball but can only boot the ball into row Z to jeers from the home fans.

Aina launches a long throw-in from the right and it’s headed behind for a corner. Trafford punches the inswinging delivery away and Williams’ effort from the edge of the box sails well over.

Forest are in their red home shirts, kicking from left to right. Leeds are in their yellow away number. Same set-up as the weekend.

Players and mascots walk on to the City Ground turf. A place in the League Cup third round on the line.

The first pre-match question put to Glasner by ITV was in relation to the reported £45m club-record deal for Chelsea forward Liam Delap. He responded: “I can tell everybody that he doesn’t play today. Everything else we shall see in the next days.”

Oliver Glasner breaks his silence on Nottingham Forest's record signing, Liam Delap 🚨He speaks to @gabrielclarke05 ahead of Forest's Carabao Cup tie against Leeds 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/8DlWMIzVS9

Reflecting on Saturday’s defeat by Leeds in his programme notes, Glasner wrote: “I saw plenty of encouraging signs from the team on Saturday and I felt we were a lot closer to scoring than we were conceding, especially in the second half. Unfortunately, the small margins were not on our side.

“I thought our defence looked comfortable, but there is still work to be done and the more the players get used to the system we’re operating, the more we’ll see that work come to fruition in competitive matches.

“We have recovered well and will be ready to give our all this evening.”

Previewing tonight’s League Cup match, Leeds head coach Daniel Farke said: “Our league win is good for our mood and confidence, but this is a ‘do or die’ cup game. Both teams will be motivated to progress, so I expect a tight game. It will be difficult to win on the road again against a tough opponent.”

When asked what winning a first trophy of his managerial career would mean to him, Farke added: “Well, we weren’t too far away last season. Overall, I would say my form in cup competitions hasn’t been too bad during my career. I’m a big believer in these competitions, I like the ‘do or die’ mentality. I would never say no to another good cup run.”

The hosts’ kits tonight will include Carabao Cup sleeve patches with the number four on them, in recognition of the club’s League Cup triumphs in 1978, 1979, 1989 and 1990.

This is Forest and Leeds Part 2, just four days after they clashed in the Premier League.

Daniel Farke ruined the Oliver Glasner welcoming party on Saturday with a 1-0 smash-and-grab victory at the death.

Both managers have gone relatively strong for this tie, with only a sprinkling of debuts.

Ousmane Diomande, the £34m signing from Sporting, makes his first appearance while there is a first start for Xaver Schlager.

Leeds have given a debut to Switzerland defender Nico Elvedi.

Nottingham Forest Sels; Diomande, Jair, Milenkovic; Aina, Schlager, Dominguez, Williams; Jesus, Kalimuendo; Wood

Subs Victor, Murillo, Abbott, Netz, Hutchinson, Ndoye, McAtee, Sangare, Hudson Odoi

Leeds United Trafford; Rodon, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Ampadu, Tanaka, Longstaff, Justin; James, Okafor; Nmecha

Subs Perri, Lienou, Bijol, Bogle, Wilson, Cresswell, Stach, Aaronson, Calvert-Lewin

The big breaking news is that Forest are smashing their club record to sign Chelsea forward Liam Delap for £45m.

Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

Welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s new head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

The Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

Daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.

#1881. Liverpool Confidential: Latest on new deals for Virgil van Dijk and Alisson as European giants circle, how Reds are trying to turbocharge academy recruitment and Joshua Abe's comeback

Published: 12:01 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 18 November 2026

European clubs are on red alert over the futures of Liverpool stars Virgil van Dijk and Alisson – despite both players being keen to extend their contracts at Anfield.

One source told me this week that AC Milan and other Italian clubs have been sniffing around Van Dijk for some time, with talks ongoing internally at those sides. Milan owner Gerry Cardinale and influential adviser Zlatan Ibrahimovic are said to be huge admirers of Van Dijk, who turns 36 next summer.

Italy was also a potential destination for Alisson last summer after Juventus held talks with his camp. At one point, Juve fancied their chances of signing him.

Both players will, as it stands, be able to negotiate a free transfer to overseas clubs from January 1, but both Alisson, 34, and Van Dijk, 35, want to stay at Anfield.

It puts the ball in the court of Julian Ward, Liverpool's sporting director, who must decide what to do next.

There had been a long-standing unwritten rule at owners Fenway Sports Group of never extending deals for those over the age of 30, but this was broken in the exceptional cases of Van Dijk and Mohamed Salah 18 months ago, after the pair led Liverpool to their 20th league title.

Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson is keen to stay at the club despite reported interest from his native Brazil

Reds captain Virgil van Dijk (right) also wants to extend his contract at Liverpool – even though AC Milan are showing interest

Despite both players wanting to stay on Merseyside, there is understandably a great deal of interest from around the world in taking them on, with local reports linking several Brazilian clubs to Alisson recently.

Van Dijk is a regular at Liverpool youth-team matches, which shows his love of the club but may also lead to suggestions the Dutchman will move into youth coaching when he does hang up his boots. He took the first-team squad to the Liverpool FC Museum recently to learn more about the club's history – further highlighting his passion for the Reds.

Interest from abroad only strengthens the hands of Alisson and Van Dijk, however, when it comes to their demands over the salary and duration of their new deals.

Alexis Mac Allister is another with an uncertain future, though his father and agent Carlos is hoping to hold talks with Liverpool in the coming weeks. The Argentine's future is less of a pressing issue for the Reds, though, given his deal runs until summer 2028.

Joe Gomez and Kostas Tsimikas are among the other players whose contracts are up in June next year.

It was around this time last year that the wheels started to fall off the Arne Slot machine. The Dutchman was eventually sacked and we have not heard much from him since. One question I am often asked is what is Slot up to – and why has he fallen off the face of the earth?

Well, I can reveal the former Reds boss is biding his time and enjoying holidays with loved ones, including several trips to Ibiza. Slot and his son Joep have also visited South America, taking in games in Argentina and Brazil.

Slot, who has also been attending matches at home, turned down the Netherlands national team job and a lucrative gig in Saudi Arabia. He also rejected approaches in the summer from clubs including AC Milan, who eventually plumped for former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim.

He is waiting for the right opportunity and does not believe his stock has fallen in the same way, for example, as several axed United or Chelsea bosses. After all, Slot won the Premier League title and would be a fine hire for most clubs around Europe.

Former Liverpool boss Arne Slot (centre, bottom row) watches the Dutch Eredivisie match between Heerenveen and his old club Feyenoord earlier this month

Slot is waiting for the right job to come up – emboldened by the knowledge he is a Premier League winner

…but AI report makes grim reading for Arne

A couple of interesting bits to pick out from the fantastic Global State of Football report by PLAIER, a firm spearheading the use of artificial intelligence in football.

Liverpool finished bottom of the table last season in PLAIER’s ranking of every team's coaches based on resources and how they performed – Regis Le Bris at Sunderland was top.

The Reds were in the bottom three for coaching efficiency, suggesting that squad quality alone is no guarantee of success. For a more in-depth look at the report, click here.

Liverpool are in the process of hiring an academy ‘talent ID lead’ to help with their youth recruitment.

Regular readers of this column will know this area is a key metric Anfield chiefs measure success by. They are now hiring someone responsible for leading the identification and recruitment of academy talent between the ages of 13 and 18 across the UK and Ireland.

Notable recent arrivals from other academies at this age include current first-teamers Rio Ngumoha, Conor Bradley, Trey Nyoni and James McConnell.

Kop Kids: Amazing Abe lights up England duty

Confidential readers will recall I revealed on October 15 that Joshua Abe was ahead of schedule in his recovery from a shoulder injury and set for just another month on the sidelines. And Abe was indeed on the pitch representing England Under 17s exactly a month later, scoring against Montenegro and then again against Poland on Saturday.

In the last 12 months, the 16-year-old has 14 goals and four assists in just over 1,200 minutes played. Those are phenomenal numbers and it would not be a surprise to see the winger back in the first-team training group again soon.

Joshua Abe has recovered from a shoulder injury and was back in action for England Under 17s this week

In the last break, the boss was spotted at the women’s Merseyside Derby. Now, he has been pictured at a local Sunday League match, taking pictures with youngsters who could not believe their luck.

These may seem like small gestures but they are a helpful way of winning hearts and minds among a fanbase whose pleas for Slot to take an active interest in all aspects of the club sometimes fell on deaf ears.

Manchester United are in town on Sunday, in case you needed reminding.

Since winning the Premier League title last year, Liverpool’s league record against the 'Big Six' is played 12, won two, drawn three, lost seven. That must improve, starting on Sunday, and there can be no excuses around a new-manager bounce for Mauricio Pochettino - who will barely have had time to find his parking space at Carrington by the time he comes to Anfield.

Liverpool need to see more from their big-money signings Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, who have been excellent for most of the season but poor in some high-profile fixtures, such as the home defeats by Manchester City and Arsenal. Across his 19 games against Liverpool, Pochettino has only won three matches, drawing five and losing 11.

Published: 14:09 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 14:19 EST, 18 November 2026

Leicester have decided to end their deal with controversial sponsors BC.GAME six months ahead of schedule.

Fans expressed fury and dismay earlier this month after the club's unlicensed gambling shirt sponsor appointed an 'international porn star' as its new ambassador.

Now Leicester have opted to conclude the partnership – in a move welcomed by supporters. A statement on Wednesday read: ‘The decision follows constructive discussions between both parties in recent days, during which we recognised our differing commercial priorities moving forward.

‘We would like to thank BC.GAME for its support throughout its two-and-a-half-year association with Leicester City and for the constructive approach taken in reaching this agreement.

‘Supporters who have purchased a BC.GAME-branded replica shirt through official LCFC retail channels within the last 28 days (since 21 October, 2026) can return it for a full refund or exchange (subject to availability) by Wednesday 2 December.’

BC.GAME, an online casino company, had been the Foxes' primary shirt sponsor since the start of the 2024-25 season. They announced a partnership with Russian adult content creator Eva Elfie in a video on X earlier this month.

Elfie, who has 4.8million Instagram followers, is known in Esports and gaming communities too

#1876. Little Common come from behind to see off Pagham

Despite falling behind early on, Common responded in excellent fashion, scoring twice before the break and adding two further goals in the second half to record a deserved victory.

Common started brightly and could have taken an early lead when Sam Ellis met a delivery into the box, only to see his header superbly saved by the visiting goalkeeper. However, it was Pagham who broke the deadlock in the 10th minute when Common failed to clear a free kick and the loose ball was scrambled home from close range.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The hosts looked for an immediate response and Ollie Hull went close to restoring parity, but his near-post effort was once again kept out by the busy Pagham goalkeeper.

Common's persistence was rewarded in spectacular fashion in the 23rd minute when Ollie MacDonald collected possession some 30 yards from goal before unleashing a thunderous strike that flew beyond the helpless goalkeeper and into the roof of the net.

The equaliser sparked Common into life and they soon completed the turnaround. Lewis Unwin delivered an inviting free kick into the penalty area, where Kieran Ludlow rose highest to guide a perfectly placed header into the far corner of the net.

Ludlow then demonstrated his importance at the opposite end, producing a vital goal-line clearance as Pagham searched for an equaliser.

Common had a golden opportunity to extend their advantage on the stroke of half-time when they were awarded a penalty. However, Hull saw his spot kick saved and appeared to be pulled down as he attempted to reach the rebound, only for the referee to wave away the appeals.

The hosts continued to look dangerous after the interval and extended their lead in the 57th minute. Excellent work from Hull down the left flank saw him deliver the ball across goal for Freddie Warren, who was on hand to tap home from close range.

Warren almost doubled his tally shortly afterwards when his effort crashed against the crossbar, while substitute Sonny Tyrell also went close after bursting into the penalty area, only to be denied by another fine save from the visiting goalkeeper. At the other end, Matt Cruttwell enjoyed a relatively quiet afternoon as Common defended resolutely and restricted Pagham to very few clear-cut opportunities.

Common put the icing on the cake in the 90th minute when Hull, who had been a constant threat throughout, once again turned provider. His pass found Tyrell on the edge of the penalty area and the substitute made no mistake, firing a powerful effort into the roof of the net to complete an emphatic victory.

Boss Russ Eldridge said: “It was a massive three points for us and I felt we thoroughly deserved the win. Going behind early on was disappointing, particularly from a set piece, but the lads showed great character to respond in the way they did.

“We scored some excellent goals, particularly Ollie MacDonald’s strike, a fantastic effort. We looked dangerous going forward and, in truth, could have scored a few more.

“What pleased me most was the attitude and work rate. We’ve put in some really spirited performances against sides near the top of the table recently without getting rewards, so it was important we backed those up with three points.

“We know there’s still plenty of hard work ahead of us, but hopefully this result will give everyone a bit of confidence and something to build on. The challenge now is to put a run of results together.”

Common host Midhurst on Saturday (Nov 28).

#1872. Rangers driven by Premier Sports Cup final carrot as Fir Park late show ignites super-charged trophy belief

Derek McInnes insists the prospect of lifting the Premier Sports Cup in the coming weeks has his squad operating with laser-like focus, with Saturday’s dramatic late victory over Motherwell providing a further boost to their growing belief that trophies are within reach.

There is still plenty of work to be done before the Rangers can contemplate silverware, but McInnes believes a shot at Hampden glory is acting as an added incentive for his players and is helping to drive standards inside the dressing room.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Before their return trip to the national stadium on December 13, Rangers must navigate a favourable-looking sequence of home fixtures, with Aberdeen, Falkirk and Dundee United all due to visit Ibrox over the next eight days in the Scottish Premiership.

While the cup final represents an obvious carrot and a major opportunity for silverware is fast approaching, McInnes knows it is impossible for his players to ignore the occasion altogether. However, he is equally determined to ensure their focus remains on the immediate task in hand, claiming performances over the next four league fixtures could determine who earns the right to feature when the big occasion arrives.

Speaking after his side kept their Premiership title assault firmly on track with a last-gasp success at Fir Park, McInnes said: “I don't think I'll mention it too often, but they are not daft, they see that and everybody wants to play in the team. Anybody who's in the team needs to keep playing well to stay in the team and anybody who's not in the team needs to train right and take advantage of their minutes.

“We make that point often enough. Sometimes you've got to come away to tough venues like Motherwell and do the hard work and get the reward, but there's bigger games like a cup final looming, so everybody wants to play in that one. I'm sure it does us no harm. It keeps the fans bubbling along, a chance of silverware, so when it comes along hopefully we're in good form.”

If the celebrations following Ryan Naderi’s scrappy 88th-minute winner against the Steelmen were anything to go by, a turbo-charged belief is surging through the Rangers ranks as they look to end a two-season trophy drought.

Such resilience is invaluable in a title challenge and McInnes is encouraged by that quality, but stressed the need for greater consistency in his side’s performance levels leading to those decisive moments.

“I think we're the only team in the Premier League who's not lost away from home, but we understand that draws won't get the job done,” he stated. “Last-minute winners are brilliant. They're normally aligned with successful teams and they can get so many points from that. It's good to know that we've got that but, like I say, I wouldn't want to be depending on it far too often.”

The importance of Rangers’ upcoming run of home fixtures is not lost on McInnes. While the jubilant scenes at full-time in North Lanarkshire were particularly satisfying, there was little time to revel in the celebrations with Aberdeen arriving at Ibrox on Tuesday night.

The Dons will venture back down the A90 in buoyant mood after giving new boss Mario Frick a winning start to his Pittodrie tenure with a 4-2 victory over bottom club Kilmarnock at the weekend.

The long-standing rivalry between the clubs leaves McInnes in no doubt that his side face another demanding test against his former club. Nevertheless, he is relishing a return to familiar surroundings after a run of five consecutive away matches.

He is equally aware, however, that home advantage alone offers no guarantee of success.

“It's unusual with five games now away from Ibrox, four in the league and the cup game, and now the fixtures kind of run the other way,” McInnes said. “We've got some good fixtures at home but we always look at little blocks in the week, and where we're looking to try and get to by a certain period, get certain points and certain targets.

“There was obviously a lot of joy and pleasure with that [Motherwell result], but it wasn't over the top. When we spoke after the game, it was about getting ourselves ready for Aberdeen. We all know the historical rivalry between both clubs. I’m sure they'll come to Ibrox with a bit of confidence getting the result [against Kilmarnock]. We need to be ready for that.

“We’ve got a big week ahead of us. and we've got to make sure we're a strong home team again. Hopefully we can score a few more goals but, ultimately, as long as we win the game I'll be happy.”

#1871. ‘Like him a lot’: Celtic star attracting interest ahead of January transfer window

Celtic midfielder Benjamin Nygren is on the radar of Atalanta and Bologna, according to reports in Italy.

Nygren joined Celtic from FC Nordsjaelland in the summer of 2025 for a fee in the region of £1.5 million and made a big impact, scoring 21 goals across all competitions as the champions retained their Premiership crown and also lifted the Scottish Cup.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The 25-year-old also represented Sweden earlier this year at the World Cup and remains an integral part of Graham Potter’s international squad.

This season, Nygren has netted eight times in 21 games. And with the January transfer window approaching, it is understood that two Serie A clubs in Atalanta and Bologna are weighing up a bid for Nygren.

Respected Italian transfer journalist Gianluca di Marzio has claimed in an interview with Rekatochklart that a move could be made for Nygren on the back of his performances over the past 18 months,

“Nygren is a very good player and Atalanta like him a lot, but they haven’t made a move for him yet,” said Di Marzio. “He is a target and they are following him.

“Bologna like him too, but no negotiations have started yet. They follow him because he is doing very well both for Celtic and Sweden.”

Bologna have taken an active interest over the past few years in the Scottish market, signing defender Aaron Hickey from Hearts and midfielder Lewis Ferguson from Aberdeen.

Atalanta were also very interested in Matt O’Riley before the Celtic midfielder moved to Brighton and Hove Albion rather than Serie A in 2024.

Nygren admitted in September that there was interest in him after the World Cup this summer, although nothing materialised for the Swede.

“Yeah, there was interest,” he said. “Was it more than that? No, I play for a big club. When the right time is to move on, I cannot answer that. That’s up to me, the club and the potential club. So whenever the right time is, it is.

“I play for a huge club like Celtic. I really enjoy being here. I wanted to stay here to play in the biggest competition. Unfortunately, we didn’t make it to the Champions League, but we still play in the Europa League. I want to make it better here and then go further in the Europa League that we did last season.

“I wanted to stay here and continue to make it good and when the right time is, the right time is. But it’s not something I think of now. It’s not my focus. My focus is just to do as well as possible here and to win more trophies and then what happens in the future, we’ll see.”

Nygren is contracted to Celtic until 2030 and the Premiership leaders would likely demand a hefty fee for his services.

#1870. Savio scores on debut as Spurs cruise past Charlton in Carabao Cup

It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest big-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his new club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

“A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

“We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

In the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

“We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi said. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”

Cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

Buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”

Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

The victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi said: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

“Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against big teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”

A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

“I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”

Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

“We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones said. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most important.”

#1869. Mourinho offers Endrick hope to Milan: “Real Madrid are more important than him”

Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho gave a strong response when asked about the potential that Endrick could leave.

In the past few days, it has been reported that Endrick could leave Los Blancos in the January transfer window. Not only that, but Real Madrid are apparently opening up to the idea of a permanent sale, with sources in Brazil stating that Milan are ready to offer a €70m package to get him.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

There have also been indications that the Spanish giants want to include a buy-back clause of €80m (as they did with Como for Nico Paz in the summer), but in amongst all of this Mourinho seems to be the one opposing any kind of exit for the 20-year-old.

Mourinho spoke at a press conference and he was asked about about the future of Endrick, admitting that the decision to let him leave may come from his superiors. MilanNews relayed his response.

“I love Endrick, and Real Madrid are more important than him. We need Endrick here and Real Madrid coach needs Endrick here,” he began.

“This is the answer to those who write things and agents. Then if the club decides other things, I respect that. But for me, as Real Madrid coach, Endrick is important. I need him.”

The ‘agents’ that Mourinho is referring to could well be Endrick’s entourage, who have given comments suggesting that a move is being explored, while they reportedly visited Milano in recent days too.

#1868. Two Scottish stadiums land World Cup matches as UK wins bid for 2035 Women’s finals

Hampden and Easter Road are set to host Women’s World Cup matches after England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales were confirmed as the joint hosts of the 2035 edition of the tournament.

The four-nation bid was given the official seal of approval in a vote by acclamation at an Extraordinary FIFA Congress on Monday, having been the sole valid bid in contention for the event.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It will be the first men’s or women’s World Cup finals to be staged in the UK since the 1966 men’s tournament was held in England.

Nineteen stadiums are proposed, with 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland and two in Wales in a tournament which will feature 48 teams. One of those venues – Old Trafford – has been included in its current guise but any rebuilt stadium is envisaged to be a host.

A further three stadiums could be added – Birmingham’s new Powerhouse Stadium, Wrexham’s redeveloped Racecourse Ground and a potential new Chelsea stadium – which would take the tournament to 16 cities and 22 stadiums across the four nations.

Scotland have two Candidate Stadiums - the national football arena Hampden (capacity 52,032), which was used as part of the delayed Euro 2020 men’s tournament in 2021, and Easter Road, the home of Hibs with a capacity of 20,093, that has never been used for a major tournament.

The bid team projected the tournament would attract 3.5 billion viewers worldwide, and that 4.5 million tickets would be sold.

FIFA’s evaluation of the bid, published earlier this month, rated it 4.3 out of five.

The Congress also approved the joint bid by Mexico, the United States, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031 finals, which will be the first to feature 48 teams.

Commenting on confirmation that Scotland will co-host the FIFA Women's World Cup 2035, First Minister John Swinney said:

"This is fantastic news for Scotland. We have proved time and again that we are a world-class host, and I am delighted that the FIFA Women's World Cup 2035 will be held in Scotland alongside England, Wales and Northern Ireland.

“The timing is ideal. Project 2035, our new long-term plan to grow the girls' and women's game, aims to establish Scotland as a leading nation for women's football by 2035. Our newly established girls’ and women’s football taskforce will help to make this happen, capitalising on the World Cup and leaving a lasting legacy for communities across the country.

“Scotland is building a remarkable reputation for hosting major events, and the FIFA Women’s World Cup joins the Tour de France Grand Départ, The Open, the World Rally Championships and UEFA EURO 2028 in promising to showcase what our country has to offer. We will make sure each one of these amazing sporting events delivers for our economy, supporting jobs, businesses and tourism.”

English Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt addressed the Congress after the bid’s success had been confirmed.

“Thank you for your trust and confidence in awarding us the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2035,” Hewitt said.

“We’re deeply honoured by your support and grateful for the opportunity to host the pinnacle of women’s football on behalf of the global football family.

“As we said throughout our bid, we want this to be your FIFA Women’s World Cup, a World Cup for everyone.

“Together, we will celebrate the power of women’s football, inspire the next generation, and unite fans from every corner of the world. We look forward to welcoming you to the United Kingdom in 2035 and just as importantly, to working closely with you all in the years ahead to deliver an exceptional FIFA Women’s World Cup that the entire football community can be proud of.”

#1867. Scotland’s World Cup award can be game-changing for the nation

Scotland captain Caroline Weir says the country being named as a host nation for the 2035 Women’s World Cup is a “pivotal moment” for the sport.

The United Kingdom’s four-nation bid was given the official seal of approval in a vote by acclamation at an Extraordinary FIFA Congress on Monday, having been the sole valid bid in contention for the event.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Nineteen stadiums are proposed, with 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland and two in Wales in a tournament which will feature 48 teams.

While the 2022 European Championships were held in England, Scotland has never hosted a major women’s football event. Hampden Park in Glasgow (capacity 52,032) and Hibs’ Easter Road in Edinburgh (capacity 20,093) are Scotland’s Candidate Stadiums and would stage at least group-stage matches. Weir feels that having the competition on Scotland’s doorstep will show youngsters in this country that “anything is possible”.

Midfielder Weir, who currently plays for Lyon and has won 122 caps for Scotland, said: “Hosting the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup in the UK is a pivotal moment for women’s football in this country. Playing at the 2019 Women’s World Cup in France was an incredible moment in my career, so knowing that the next generation of Scottish players will have the chance to experience that on home soil is so special.

“The women's game in Scotland has so much potential and this tournament is a real opportunity to drive momentum and help take it to another level both nationally and internationally.

“For young girls and boys across the country, seeing the best players in the world right on their doorstep will show them that anything is possible.

“We’re so proud to play our part in welcoming the world in 2035 and I know I speak on behalf of all of the players and staff when I say that we are ready to rise to the challenge and help deliver a truly memorable, world-class tournament.”

Scottish Football chief executive Ian Maxwell hailed the decision to award the event to the UK. “Securing the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup alongside our Home Nations partners is a momentous milestone for Scottish football,” he said. “Scotland has a proud footballing heritage and a rapidly growing women’s game, and welcoming the world to Barclays Hampden and Easter Road will turbo-charge the progress we have made across our grassroots, domestic, and international game.

“This tournament will be the single-biggest sporting event ever staged in the UK, and our ambition goes far beyond the matches themselves. It gives us a powerful platform to inspire participation in a new generation of girls and women across Scotland, empower more female leaders and match officials and deliver a sustainable commercial and community legacy for many years to come.”

It will be the first time that Easter Road, the home of Hibs, has been selected to host a major international event and the club say they are hugely excited at the prospect.

Hibs Women’s head coach Joelle Murray said: “This is fantastic news for women's football in Scotland and something we should all be extremely excited about.

“To welcome the best players in the world to Easter Road would be incredibly special and provide a brilliant opportunity to showcase the women's game. It would also give young girls across the country the chance to experience a World Cup on their doorstep and to see what is possible to achieve through football.

“Having played and coached at Easter Road throughout my career, it holds a very special place in my heart. To see it named as a Candidate Stadium for a Women's World Cup is a hugely proud moment for me, and the opportunity to inspire the next generation makes it even more exciting.”

Hibs chief executive Dan Barnett added: “The inclusion of Easter Road as a Candidate Stadium for the 2035 FIFA Women's World Cup is fantastic news for the Club and the City of Edinburgh.

"This is something we've been working hard on for several months, with various positive discussions with the Scottish FA and key stakeholders. In recent years, we have been delighted to host Scotland Women's National Team matches at Easter Road, so to be named as a Candidate Stadium for the finals in 2035 is a huge honour.

“To have the opportunity to showcase our stadium on the world's biggest stage would be an immensely proud moment for the Club. It presents a unique opportunity to welcome tens of thousands of supporters from across the world to Edinburgh and create a lasting legacy for the women's game.

"We're excited by the next steps and the prospect of working alongside the Scottish FA, the City of Edinburgh Council and our partners to help bring this opportunity to life.”

The bid team projected the tournament would attract 3.5 billion viewers worldwide, and that 4.5 million tickets would be sold. FIFA’s evaluation of the bid, published earlier this month, rated it 4.3 out of five.

The tournament will feature 48 nations and 104 matches across 39 days, with the final host cities and stadiums to be confirmed by FIFA in due course.

#1866. Vincent Kompany to RETURN to Bayern dugout less than a month after collapsing at training ground: Club chief reveals 'meningeal irritation' has fully 'healed'

Published: 14:59 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 15:01 EST, 18 November 2026

Bayern Munich's chief executive has confirmed Vincent Kompany is expected to return to the dugout on Friday, less than a month after collapsing at the club's training ground.

Kompany collapsed on October 23 while watching Bayern's Under-23 side and reportedly suffered from seizures.

The 40-year-old, who suffered a dislocated shoulder in the fall, underwent tests in hospital which determined that a 'meningeal irritation' had been the cause of his collapse.

If left untreated meningeal irritation can become meningitis. The meninges are the membranes around the brain and spinal cord.

Kompany was discharged from hospital the following week to continue his recovery at home.

The Belgian coach is now set to return to the dugout when Bayern face Cologne on Friday, with Kompany due to also address the media tomorrow morning.

Vincent Kompany is set to return to the Bayern Munich dugout for their Bundesliga match on Friday

Kompany's return was officially confirmed by Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen.

'Yes, Vincent is in pretty good spirits. I ran into him today,' Dreesen told German outlet Abendzeitung.

'The meningeal irritation has healed. He has already undergone shoulder surgery.'

Kompany had led training for the first time since his collapse earlier this week, with his arm reportedly in a sling following his shoulder injury.

He had missed five matches during his recovery with Bayern winning two and drawing against Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga.

The German champions also beat Atletico Madrid in the Champions League in his absence, as well as progressing in the DFB Cup.

Kompany's assistant Aaron Danks had overseen the first team during his recovery.

Danks previously worked as Kompany's assistant at Anderlecht before deputising for Dean Smith and Steven Gerrard at Aston Villa and Michael Carrick at Middlesbrough.

Kompany has missed five matches following his collapse at Bayern's training ground on October 23

Bayern had stressed they wanted to give Kompany as much time as required to recover before returning to work.

The German giants play eight matches in the next month, including two matches in the Champions League, before the Bundesliga takes its winter break.

Reports had emerged after Kompany's collapse that club officials had been concerned by his irregular eating habits, as well as barely exercising, drinking excessive amounts of coffee, and taking on too much work.

Bayern sporting director Max Eberl dismissed the claims last month, reiterating that Kompany's illness had been the cause of his collapse rather than his workload.

The Hibees have not won a league game on their own turf since defeating Kilmarnock 3-0 in early April and their supporters turned on them during a grim 4-0 defeat by Dundee United on Saturday that left them second bottom of the table.

If they fail to beat Dundee on Tuesday, the winless streak in Leith will extend beyond the eight-month mark.

“I don’t know,” said midfielder McGrath on why he thought they were struggling for results at Easter Road. “Personally, I always like playing at home. I love the pitch, I love the stadium. It’s a big open pitch, which I think should suit us. But for whatever reason, so far this season we haven’t been able to capitalise on playing at home.

“It’s hard to put your finger on one certain thing. After a difficult start to the season which resulted in Marink Reedijk replacing David Gray as manager in late September, it looked like Hibs had turned the corner when they followed up a rousing victory over city rivals Hearts in the Premier Sports Cup semi-final with a 4-0 win at Aberdeen in their last game before the international break.

McGrath, therefore, is hopeful Saturday’s aberration will prove a blip. “We’ve been on a decent run the last month and probably the international break came at a tricky time for us,” said the Republic of Ireland international. Or not a tricky time, but we were just kind of building momentum and had two good wins back-to-back against two good teams.

“It’s frustrating not to build on that, but hopefully we can put Saturday down to a bad day and get back on track.”

McGrath is unfazed by Hibs being 11th in the table as he senses a chance to change that with three matches in the space of nine days against other sides in the bottom six.

“It’s not something that we’re concerned about at the minute,” he said. “It’s obviously not where we want to be.

“We want to try to get closer to that top six and this two-week period is quite crucial in terms of there being nine points in the next week up for grabs. If you put a little run together, you can boost yourself right up the league.

“It’s just about finding that consistency to hopefully propel us up the league.”

“Milan are keeping in touch with the player, his departure in January is possible, the doors are open if necessary. Then we need to understand the conditions, the prices, it’s clear that Sporting isn’t just interested in giving away a player like that for any price.

#1860. Ian Hart: Let’s keep Brighton’s defeat to Tigers in perspective – and get back on the horse quickly

No matter how much possession you have or how many chances you create, or what the xG is (whatever that is!), unless you put the ball over the line more times than your opponents, it ultimately counts for nothing.

But while Sunday’s defeat at Hull City wasn’t pleasant viewing, perhaps in almost a perverse way it might be the wake-up call the Albion needed.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Let’s admit it, in the lead-up to the most recent international break, we were almost getting carried away. Full disclosure I, among thousands of others, was secretly daring to dream, maybe not the title, but the words Champions and League had entered old Harty’s thought process.

And to be fair that wasn’t just from within the club and its fanbase, externally, Brighton were being lauded as legitimate title contenders.

While attending an excellent Seagulls Down Under function in Adelaide, one of the Albion’s ever-growing Aussie contingent showed me an online tabloid story stating that Brighton would be head to head with defending Champions Arsenal for the League!

Some weeks ago I wrote that I felt Albion more suited to the role of ‘EPL ‘andlords’ in that while they might not win the title, along with the likes of Bournemouth and Brentford they would ultimately dictate the outcome of the competition.

And after Sunday, that might also apply at the other end of the table.

Prior to kick-off, Hull City only had Manchester United below them in the form table. While there are still 27 games to go, that last-gasp and – many might argue – somewhat fortunate win for the Tigers, might be the difference between success and failure come the end of the season.

Given the Albion should have been home and hosed by half-time, it is extremely annoying, but it’s football.

And the next 270 minutes, with the Albion playing three games in seven days – the Conference League home tie against Romania’s Universitatea Craiova on Thursday night, before league games on Sunday and Wednesday, Newcastle at home and Bournemouth away – I believe we will see and learn more about the character of Fabian Hurzeler and his squad.

With those games and the welcome return of the talismanic Kaoru Mitoma from his long-term injury, it’s very much of a case of getting back on the horse immediately and moving forward again.

I do wonder how much the attendance on Thursday will be affected by the 5.45pm kick-off time, to accommodate the TV companies. However perhaps on the flip.side with it being a ‘school night’ with a sensible ticket pricing policy we might see a number of the next generation of young Albion fans attending the Amex for the first time.

We will know the answer to that around 7pm Thursday and hopefully by then the Albion will be well on the way to returning to winning ways.

As a footnote, and another opportunity to put things firmly into perspective, Sunday’s game on Humberside was a couple of weeks short of the 30th anniversary of perhaps one of the most memorable Brighton v Hull fixtures.

Saturday, December 14, 1996 – Steve Gritt’s first game as Albion manager, with his new charges firmly rooted to the bottom of the entire Football League.

Anti-Gritt graffiti outside the ground (with his name spelt wrong!), a fans’ protest involving 3,000 whistles to put the poor old ref on the back foot, but in the end a 3-0 and ‘The Great Escape’ was on!

So all these years later, despite Sunday’s defeat, the Albion are still second in the Premier League doesn’t seem that bad.

The 53-year-old has had little time to ponder his future. Dundee are back in action as soon as Tuesday night at Easter Road against Hibs, who are themselves hurting following a 4-0 home defeat against Dundee United in their last outing. "It has been a tough 24, 48 hours," said Pressley. "There’s a lot of embarrassment, a lot of disappointment."

He stressed there was also a determination to learn from the most challenging experience of his managerial career. Although he has spoken before of coming close to walking away on at least two occasions last season, resigning had not crossed his mind this time.

“Not this weekend, no,” he said. “I've had to find strength from I don't know where, but not this weekend. Not this weekend. But it was hugely embarrassing.

“It probably ranks as the most embarrassing moment of my managerial career thus far.

“I'm 17, 18 years into my coaching career and it's why, in football, you can never become complacent.

“Because nothing ever surprises you. You think you've lived through everything, and then something else comes along. And very much that was Saturday.”

Pressley has admitted considering quitting after disappointing results in his first season at Dundee, one of which was a 4-0 defeat at Pittodrie against Aberdeen. Dundee recovered from a poor start to the campaign and Pressley succeeded in getting his critics firmly on side.

However, the historic nature of Saturday’s result meant he found himself under fire again from some quarters. Pressley has resolved to find the answers. Dundee will be without key defender Owen Bevan, who was sent off on Saturday night, against Hibs.

The club have decided against appealing the decision. “We accept the punishment,” said Pressley. “It is not ideal but I don’t think there was a real chance of it being overturned.”

Pressley suggested there would not be a radical overhaul of the side or system. “It is difficult to change a lot in two days so we have to be very careful," he said. "But we have thought a lot about what we can do. There has to be a change in (the suspended) Owen Bevan. There is a lot to consider. But the most important thing is we give a response and try to get some level of pride back.”

#1857. Nightmare at Dens Park: Dundee come to terms with history as child asks ‘what about last night?’

It wasn’t quite the morning after the night before. Nevertheless, Dundee players were very obviously still bearing the mental scars on Monday nearly 48 hours after a night of infamy inflicted by Hearts.

An old adage is that it’s best to go again as quickly as possible to get the performance and - most urgently of all – the result out of the system.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

“To a point, yes…” agreed Steven Pressley when this theory was put to him at the sun-sprayed Dundee training facility at Gardyne College Campus ahead of Tuesday’s return to action against Hibs.

The counter argument, one the Dundee manager was clearly conscious of, is that three nights later is maybe just a bit too soon. In addition, when it comes to grounds Dundee might choose to visit for their next assignment after losing 8-0 – or should that be 0-8 – then Easter Road would not be high on the list. Dundee have not won there for a quarter of a century. The record books are being well-thumbed just now.

“We obviously don’t have a lot of time to work on elements of our game plan,” said Pressley. “It has been pretty frantic.

“Not only have we had to plan how we have to play and be prepared for Hibernian, I have also had to think a lot about the management of the group and everybody within that. I have had to find a way to stabilise the group.”

The employment of such words as “stabilise” reflect the harrowing nature of the experience. A group of 16 players including substitutes, many of them in their early 20s, endured something akin to a medical procedure.

A rampant Hearts side removed their sense of self-belief with almost surgical precision. Professional sport is often about how quickly such wounds can heal.

But this is new territory for everyone, including those as steeped in the game as Pressley. Owen Goodman, the 22-year-old keeper on loan from Crystal Palace, was perhaps left with most to feel sore about on Saturday night as goal after goal whizzed past him.

Dundee presumably have a duty of care towards him. It’s maybe one reason why Pressley decided against showing a re-run of the match the following morning. “I didn’t think putting them through the agony of watching it again was helpful,” he said.

Goodman was the last Dundee player to leave the field and one of the first in on Monday. He mentioned never having let in eight goals before, even in academy games. This was new territory for so many.

Young men such as Goodman carry a huge burden of responsibility as they attempt to bounce back from a historic defeat. An updated edition of the definitive Dundee FC history book, They Wore the Dark Blue, has just been published. It’s already out of date in one respect. Although it contains every result, competitive and otherwise, dating back to 1893, the Dundee fans' bible doesn’t include what now stands as the club’s biggest-ever home loss.

Such landmark results usually belong in the late 1800s, rendered a curiosity rather than a wounding detail due to the passage of time.

In Dundee’s case, prior to Saturday, their biggest-ever home defeat was relatively recent – 1971, against a Celtic side who had been crowned European champions in recent enough memory for one newspaper to describe them having “conjured the magic of Lisbon” at Dens Park following their 8-1 win.

Aberdeen equalled the margin of victory if not the scoreline in 2017. But Hearts outdid both those results on Saturday night. When Stuart Findlay rose like Alan Gilzean to nod in No 8 with a minute or so of the game left, the old pillars in the Dens Park main stand might have warped a fraction in recognition of the goal’s significance. Even if few, least of all Findlay, were probably aware of it at the time. A historic low dating back to 1893 – 1899 in the case of Dens Park itself – had been recorded.

Extraordinary, unthinkable results do happen. Just ask Hearts. Five goals down to Falkirk at home just a few weeks ago, they at least rallied to 5-2. Rallying was something Dundee conspicuously failed to do, which might have been the most disappointing aspect of the night for Pressley personally. He shouldered the blame himself, citing his suspicion that a poor performance had been in the post. He just didn't realise how poor. When he sought to rectify things at half time by sending on three substitutes there was precious little reaction. If anything things got worse, with Dundee reduced to ten men due to Owen Bevan’s red card.

Often teams who rack up handsome half-time leads cannot maintain such intensity in the second half due to a combination of factors, including stiff resolve from the opposition to avoid further embarrassment. This wasn’t evident on Saturday. Hearts scored another four goals to match their first-half quota and might have scored more, with another chalked off for a handball.

Although he says he did not consider tendering his resignation, it’s safe to assume Pressley endured a long dark night of the soul on Saturday night when he returned home to Edinburgh.

He said he found strength “from I don’t know where” and has been buoyed from a raft of messages of support. Perhaps Drey Wright, the Dundee wing-back, got to the heart of what it all meant on a human level.

“My six-year-old was at home watching the game, getting very upset with every goal that's going in,” said the 30-year-old.

“My eight-year-old is putting his hand on the shoulder of my wife, kind of subconsciously helping her out. So that's not easy to hear.

“I was back in training yesterday and later I was at the dinner table and my eldest says: ‘So Dad, what about that score last night?’ And it’s this kind of a back-to-reality moment. There’s no getting away from it.”

#1856. Footy Headlines: Emirates to adapt shirt logo ahead of 2027-28 season

AC Milan’s shirt sponsor Emirates are set to make a change ahead of the 2027-28 season, according to a report.

As per Footy Headlines, the ‘Fly Better’ text will be removed from the shirts of Arsenal, Real Madrid and Milan ahead of next season. Instead, the airline will simply display the word ‘Emirates’ across the middle of the clubs that they sponsor.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As mentioned, it will not take effect immediately and will be something that is adopted from next season. The ‘Fly Better’ tagline started being seen in 2020 as a new marketing slogan that replaced the iconic ‘Fly Emirates’.

The idea is to create a more ‘streamlined’ look on the kits, and that is also why we have been seeing leaked designs for next season that feature just the singular word.

Of course, this is not the only alteration from a kit perspective that Milan are gearing up for. In case you missed the big news of the past few weeks, Adidas are set to take over from PUMA ahead of 2028-29, for what will be a fourth stint as the manufacturer of the Rossoneri’s shirts.

It is believed to be a record-breaking deal at least in Serie A, one that will net the club around €500m over the duration of the agreement. For many, it is a welcome return to a brand that became synonymous with Milan given the length of their last stint as the kit maker.

#1855. Bridges show fighting spirit to secure vital victory

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

After nine games in all competitions without a victory, Three Bridges finally showed signs of life, securing a much-needed 2-1 win over Cheshunt in what was a crucial encounter for their survival hopes.

Following a more encouraging performance against Dartford on Tuesday evening, Bridges knew that nothing less than three points would do if they were to stand any chance of remaining a Step 3 side next season. And it was the home side who started on the front foot, dominating much of the first half and creating a number of opportunities. Noel Leighton, Reece Hallard, Hayden Velvick and Charlie Bennett all went close inside the opening 25 minutes, but none could find a way past Cheshunt goalkeeper Rex Porter.

Against the run of play, however, the visitors took the lead. Hayden Neathey conceded a needless free-kick just outside the penalty area, and Joe Re stepped up to curl the ball past Sam Roberts. That familiar sinking feeling descended over Jubilee Field, and despite having enjoyed the better of the half, Bridges went into the interval a goal behind.

But this time, there was no heads dropping. Bridges continued where they had left off, and their positive approach was eventually rewarded.

After seeing an attempted lob saved by Porter, Leighton and his teammates finally found a way through, with the lively HAYDEN VELVICK restoring parity. Picking up the ball on the right-hand side of the penalty area, the winger unleashed an effort which somehow found its way past Porter at his near post. However it went in, nobody in amber and black was complaining, and Bridges were back on level terms.

The hosts continued to press for a winner, and debutant Jadyn Dundas should have put them ahead just minutes after coming off the bench. Arriving at the back post with the goal at his mercy, he was unable to get his feet sorted out in time to convert. What then followed was an end-to-end contest, with Sam Granville striking the crossbar for Cheshunt before Leighton and Velvick both saw efforts bravely blocked by visiting defenders.

This time, though, Bridges were not to be denied. Cheshunt failed to deal with the danger inside their own penalty area, and after Porter could only parry an initial deflected effort, the ball fell kindly into the path of NOEL LEIGHTON. The striker made no mistake from close range, sending Jubilee Field into celebration and, more importantly, putting Bridges 2-1 ahead.

The home side looked relatively comfortable heading towards the final whistle, but injury time brought one final scare. An almighty scramble inside the Bridges six-yard box threatened to produce a late Cheshunt equaliser, with the visitors seemingly doing everything they could to force the ball over the line. Somehow, the Bridges defence stood firm and managed to clear their lines before the referee finally blew for full-time.

There was an enormous sigh of relief around Jubilee Field as Three Bridges secured just their third league victory of the season. A hugely important result for Jamie Crellin's side, and one which could prove to be a turning point in their season.

If the great escape is to become a reality, Jubilee Field must now become a fortress, starting next Saturday afternoon when Wingate & Finchley visit for another crucial encounter.

Bridges team: Roberts, Ferreira, J Hallard (Irving 75), Adeyinka, Neathey, Leighton (C), R Hallard (Dundas 65), Malone, Saunders, Velvick, Bennett (Idowu-Johnson 87)

The Dockers seemed to gain a greater boost from their win as they put Lancing under pressure for long periods. The margin could easily have been greater had Newhaven not wasted some good opportunities, while Lancing failed to give home keeper Ethan Pike much of a test.

It began ominously – as early as the second minute Scott Packer had to show his defensive qualities to prevent a threat and concede a corner, injuring himself in the process.After treatment from physio Callum Morin, he resumed.

Minutes later the Dockers were in front. The first of a number of dangerous long throws was not properly cleared and the ball found its way to Lee Robinson, unmarked on the edge of the six-yard box. The veteran goal ace found the net with aplomb.

Lancing’s first attempt came as a result of a free-kick for a foul on Mo Khedidji. The ball was laid square to him but his effort on goal flew over.

This was followed almost immediately by Lancing’s best move. Emmanuel N’cho wove his way cleverly down the right ,slipping the ball through to Jay Popham, who fired low into the corner to level the scores with 11 minutes gone.

But soon Lancing were punished by a far-post header from Matt Gunn, restoring their lead. Two further chances from the Dockers went begging.

Newhaven were keeping up the pressure and it needed a superb block tackle by Oliver Deda to halt a run towards the Lancing goal. Lancing were conceding corners which were proving difficult for Elliot Dailey to hold on to as he was being obstructed and forced to attempt to punch clear.

Lancing kept battling but could not capitalise on their possession.

The second half began with Lancing inches from an equaliser. Antoine Sharpe showed again what a threat his pace is.

The ball was sent deep down the Dockers left. Sharpe chased it down with Pike in hot pursuit from his goal-line to attempt to clear the ball into touch.Sharpe got there first and with the goal gaping he tried to reach the net from a very tight angle. But the ball struck the near post.

Lancing went close again when Packer got on the end of a free kick and attempted to lob the keeper from close range but his effort lacked height.

Isaac Brown, returning from injury, replaced Rob Deda with Oliver Deda switching to the left of defence.

But in the 78th minute.Billy Oliver shrugged of a few challenges and powered his way through before lifting the ball into the net.

The Dockers came close to a fourth with a header from a free-kick which went wide.

Lancing brought on Dylan Hurst and Dylan Walter for Popham and McGonigleand almost pulled one back when Oliver Deda turned sharply at the edge of the box and fired in a shot that was deflected for a corner.

So for Lancing, a case of After the Lord Mayor’s Show. They remain in 14th place on17 points and visit AFC Varndeanians on Saturday.
